items.description: An MobileGestalt editor for iOS 27.x, featuring region-code tweaks, device presets, backups.
items.readme:
GestaltX

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.3-blue)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-27.x-black?logo=apple)](#compatibility) [![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-SwiftUI-orange?logo=swift)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv3-blue)](LICENSE) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_ZH-CN.md) A MobileGestalt editor for iPhone and iPad. Developed by [huamidev](https://github.com/huamidev). ## Features | Category | Presets and tools | | --- | --- | | Display | Dynamic Island capability and layout, Always-On Display, AOD Vibrancy, Liquid Glass low-power rendering | | Device | Model name, boot/shutdown chime, charge limit, tap to wake, Camera Control settings, Action Button settings | | iPad | Apple Pencil settings, Stage Manager capability, iPad app compatibility | | Intelligence | Independent region-code options, Apple Intelligence capability flag, and sales-region options for activation attempts on China-mainland devices | | Advanced | Apple internal feature flags, internal storage view, Security Research Device flag | | Field editor | Read, search, add, edit, and remove `CacheExtra` fields; local plist import/export; String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Data, Date, Array, and Dictionary values | | Changes | Automatic reading and manual re-read, staged before/after review, verified writes, per-preset restore | | Backups | Automatic initial backup before device editing, backup before every write, original-value records; open, export, restore, and delete | | Logs & respring | Actual exploit-stage logs and manual NeoSpring respring | Usually, changing the region code is enough to try enabling AI; there is no need to change Sales Region. Selecting United States for Region Code sets `RegionCode` to `LL` and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code. *If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.* Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added. Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. China-mainland devices can use the Apple Intelligence and region options to attempt activation; availability also depends on the model, OS version, and Apple services. ## Compatibility Supports **iOS / iPadOS 27.x**. **iOS / iPadOS 26.x is not supported for on-device MobileGestalt access.** Powered by [worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query). SystemGroup access requires iOS 27; available features depend on the device and OS. Local plist editing is also supported. Signing requires a certificate and provisioning profile with at least one usable App Group. Sign the app and its embedded share extension with at least one **common App Group**, and keep the extension when re-signing. Both processes detect their actual signed App Groups at runtime. ## Import a plist In Files or another app, select a MobileGestalt plist, tap **Share**, and choose **GestaltX**. The share extension reads the supplied file and hands it to the app through the shared App Group. Return to GestaltX if it does not open automatically. The app checks a device-bound proof from a GestaltX export, or at least two unique identifiers obtained from this device, then asks you to confirm the import. Files that cannot be verified are rejected. Previously imported files are never used as the reference for device identity. Some original plists contain no unique device identifiers. Export a copy from GestaltX on this device first: its verification key stays in the device-only Keychain and is never included in the file. Shared files are checked at launch and on return to the foreground. Pending edits are preserved until you save or discard them. Confirmed imports open as local documents. **MG Control** supports adding, editing, renaming and deleting typed keys and values. Use **Restore Imported Plist** to restore a verified file to this device; restoration requires a matching system cache layout and an additional confirmation, backs up the current file, and verifies the write. Restart the device afterward. ## Language support GestaltX follows your iOS language settings, with English as the default and fallback. Persian includes right-to-left layout support. | Language | Locale | | --- | --- | | English | `en` | | 简体中文 — Simplified Chinese | `zh-Hans` | | 繁體中文（台灣）— Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) | `zh-Hant-TW` | | 繁體中文（香港）— Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong) | `zh-Hant-HK` | | Tiếng Việt — Vietnamese | `vi` | | Русский — Russian | `ru` | | فارسی — Persian | `fa` | ## Credits - [forcequitOS / Taj C — worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query) - [neonmodder123](https://github.com/neonmodder123) - [skadz108](https://github.com/skadz108) - [rooootdev — NeoSpring](https://github.com/rooootdev/neospring) - [Nouvborne — Ketamine](https://github.com/Nouvborne/Ketamine) - [PoomSmart — MGKeys](https://github.com/PoomSmart/MGKeys) - [leminlimez — Nugget](https://github.com/leminlimez/Nugget) - [rooootdev — mond](https://github.com/rooootdev/mond) - [frs0n — GestaltEdit](https://github.com/frs0n/GestaltEdit) ## Disclaimer For security research and educational purposes only. Use only on devices you own or are authorized to manage. Back up your data before making changes. Modifying MobileGestalt may cause system instability or require a device restore. You are responsible for the changes you apply and the resulting risks. ## License [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE) · Copyright © 2026 huamidev.

items.name: NX2navi
items.readme: # NX2navi **Join the official NX2navi update discord server: https://discord.com/invite/uf6gSrsPpq** **NX2navi** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* for Nintendo Switch 2 (game version 1.1.1) into a native x86-64 application for Windows, with a Vulkan renderer ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)). > [!IMPORTANT] > **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, dumped from your own console. > Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided. > > The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it. ## Status Early development, playable. Kokiri Forest, Kakariko Village, Death Mountain Trail and its crater, the Temple of Time and the Great Fairy fountains play at 60 fps and above on current GPUs, from the title screen and from saves. Visual bugs and occasional crashes are still expected ([Known issues](#known-issues)). Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Features - Native code, not emulation - 60 fps by default, or a limit of 30 to 240 fps, the display's refresh rate or unlimited - Native widescreen and ultrawide (the window's shape, 21:9 or 32:9) with the HUD, menus and movies kept 16:9 - Game resolutions from 1080p to above the game's 1440p: 1800p, 4K, 5K or the window's own size, sharp on high-DPI displays - Upscaling and anti-aliasing: NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA, Quality, Balanced, Performance, Ultra Performance; RTX GPUs) or AMD FSR 3.1 (Native AA and the same modes; any GPU), which render the 3D scene at the mode's share and keep the HUD sharp; or AMD FSR 1 or bilinear scaling to the window, with a sharpness setting; black bars or stretch - Frame generation: NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation (RTX 40 and 50 GPUs, paced with Reflex) at 2x, or 3x and 4x on RTX 50 GPUs (one, two or three generated frames for every frame the game draws), or AMD FSR 3.1 (any GPU), a generated frame between every two the game draws, with the HUD kept out of it, for about twice the frame rate on a fast display; in a window of another shape than the picture, frames are generated inside the picture only, so the black bars stay clean. With frame generation on, the frame limit counts the frames on screen, and with no limit chosen it is the display's refresh rate. The frame limit can also be handed to RivaTuner Statistics Server - HDR on HDR displays: the game's own native HDR, or its SDR picture tone mapped to the display's peak, with exposure, highlights, shadows, contrast, saturation and gamma in the menu - The game's known shaders prepared when the game is built, and the pipelines met in play built again in the background at each start, so play rarely stops to compile them; a shader or pipeline met for the first time can still hold a frame, and a draw that must wait for its pipeline has it built on worker threads, never on the game's drawing thread - In-game settings menu (F1, or Minus and Plus together on a gamepad) and performance overlay (F10) - Keyboard, mouse and gamepads with remapping, Nintendo, Xbox or PlayStation button layout, rumble and gyro; the game follows whichever connected gamepad you press, and DualShock 3 controllers are read directly when enabled - Xbox, PlayStation and keyboard and mouse button prompts in the game's own text, drawn on your PC when the game is built; the keyboard prompts follow your key bindings - Stereo or 5.1 surround sound output, on the output device of your choice; the default microphone for the game's microphone input - The monitor the game opens on, straight in fullscreen when fullscreen is on - Your Discord status shows "Playing NX2navi" with the play time (on by default; the Game tab of the menu or the launcher's Settings turns it off) - Docked or handheld console mode - The game's textures stay compressed (BC3, about half the video memory at the same speed) unless the PC has 20 GiB of video memory and 48 GiB of RAM, as Windows counts video memory against the system's commit limit ## Installing Download `NX2navi-Setup-.exe` from the releases and start it next to your `.nup` dump. It is the only file you need. The launcher it installs finds the dump, downloads the build tools, builds the game on your PC (10 to 25 minutes, once) and starts it; afterwards it keeps the port up to date and rebuilds only what changed ([docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md)). [docs/README-BuildKit.md](docs/README-BuildKit.md) describes the same build by hand, [docs/building.md](docs/building.md) building from source. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `nx2navi.ini` ([nx2navi.ini.example](nx2navi.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md). Requirements: Windows 10 or later; an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2/FMA machines get a faster build); 16 GB of RAM; about 30 GB free for the game and 1.5 GB for the launcher and its tools; a GPU with Vulkan 1.3, `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` and `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`. The setup is not signed, so SmartScreen warns on its first start. ## Known issues - The first start after an install or update, and the first visit to an area, can pause briefly while the graphics driver builds what it has not seen; later starts are smooth. - Machines with 16 GB of RAM can run out of system memory in Hyrule Field. - Integrated AMD GPUs can fail at the title screen (their host memory heap is too small for the game's memory). - A rare crash in the game's particle code. ## License The source is public to read. Its additions and changes are all rights reserved ([LICENSE-ADDITIONS](LICENSE-ADDITIONS)): no part of them may be copied or published without written permission. The base import stays under its [MIT License](LICENSE), and third-party code keeps its own license ([THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). No license grants anything for Nintendo's game. NX2navi is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. *The Legend of Zelda*, *Ocarina of Time* and *Nintendo Switch* are trademarks of Nintendo. ## Building from source [docs/building.md](docs/building.md) lists the toolchain and the steps. `tools/make_game.py` also builds the game natively on Linux ([docs/README-BuildKit.md](docs/README-BuildKit.md), "Linux"); the launcher and the setup are Windows only. Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores; run `tools/check_content.py` before a commit.

items.name: S2Arm
items.description: Run your own Switch games natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac: game code rewritten to ARM64, graphics direct to Metal, one app for the whole library. Bring your own games and keys. 把你自己的 Switch 游戏原生带到 iPhone / iPad / Mac。
items.readme:
**Your own Switch games, running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac.** Game code is rewritten to native ARM64 and runs directly on the device's processor, with graphics going straight to Metal. Your whole library lives in one app, and a few clicks in the Mac or Windows launcher take a game from import to play. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS / iPadOS 18 and later) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later) · Build on Mac or Windows · Android / HarmonyOS coming soon · License: Apache-2.0 · **Bring your own games** [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Download the launcher](https://jhaizhou-ops.github.io/S2Arm/) · [All releases](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/releases) · [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md)

## A native port, not an emulator The game's own ARM64 code is rewritten at build time and then runs directly on the processor in your iPhone, iPad or Mac. There is no CPU emulator in between. Graphics calls are translated straight to Metal, and system services come from a native host. That is where the speed, the low heat and the battery life come from. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#native-port) ## One app, your whole library Every game you import goes into the same S2Arm app; open it and pick what to play. The whole library takes a single App slot on your developer account, so adding a game never means installing another app or spending another signing slot. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#one-app-whole-library) ## Graphical launchers, next to zero setup There is a graphical launcher for Mac and one for Windows. On first launch the welcome page boils everything down to three steps: get this computer ready, add your keys, add your games, with a single primary button at any moment. Everything else is either bundled or fetched in one click, and you never touch a command line. After you click Build, every stage shows its progress, elapsed and remaining time, and disk use. Several games can queue up and build one after another. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#graphical-launchers)

## Let an AI drive Both the Mac and Windows launchers expose a control interface, `s2armctl`. An AI assistant can import games, build, install, follow progress and read errors, and every step shows up in the launcher window. A companion self-check, self-fix and feedback toolkit lets the AI find a problem, apply the documented fix, and, when it cannot, package a diagnostic bundle for you to file. Watch an AI diagnose and fix a real problem end to end: [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#ai-at-the-wheel) ### Have an AI do it for you Send this to your AI assistant (it needs to be able to run commands on your computer): > Please read https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/blob/main/launchers/macos/skill/s2arm-operator/SKILL.md and then help me install my Switch game on my iPhone. It moves forward with a few commands, and you can watch every step in the launcher window: ```bash /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl start # open and connect to the launcher /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl next # what to do now, who does it, and why /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl diag export ~/Desktop/S2Arm-diagnostics.zip # export a diagnostic bundle if it cannot fix a problem ``` Anything only you can do (system permission prompts, signing in with your Apple ID, tapping Trust on your phone), the AI stops and asks you to do. On Windows, use `s2armctl.cmd` in the launcher folder with the same commands; exporting a diagnostic bundle is currently Mac-only. ## Tested at scale **211** games surveyed with a **95%** first-try build success rate. **4,700+** test runs on real iOS devices and **1,000+** on macOS. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#tested-at-scale) ## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery On a 16 GB MacBook Air (M3), from importing a game to a finished iPhone build, completely cold: | Game | Game files | Shaders | Build time | |---|---|---|---| | A 23.5 GB action RPG | 23.5 GB | 1,222 | **6.4 min** | | A 12.0 GB life-sim game | 12.0 GB | 9,315 | **8.6 min** | | A 17.5 GB open-world game | 17.5 GB | 26,999 | **34 min** | A Switch 2 game, measured on an iPhone 17 Pro Max: a **full 60 fps** while the phone is cool, **37–43 fps** once sustained load has heated it up, at about **0.15 J per frame**. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#speed-and-efficiency) ## Platforms | Platform | Support | |---|---| | iPhone / iPad | iOS / iPadOS 18 and later; every game is chosen inside one app | | Mac | Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later; builds locally and plays games right on the Mac | | Windows | Graphical launcher that builds and installs games for iPhone / iPad | | Android / HarmonyOS | Coming soon | [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#platforms) ## Getting started 1. Download the Mac or Windows launcher from the [download page](https://jhaizhou-ops.github.io/S2Arm/) and open it. Building for iPhone on a Mac needs the free Xcode from the App Store, signed in with your Apple ID; the launcher walks you through it. 2. Import your own keys and games. Put the base game, updates and DLC in one folder and import them together. 3. Choose iPhone / iPad or this Mac, then click Build. 4. Follow the launcher to sign and install with your own Apple ID (the Windows launcher ships with the Impactor signing tool), open S2Arm, and pick a game from the library. Back up your saves before updating the app. The release uses the new app identifier `io.s2arm.*`, which the system treats as a new app: saves from the beta builds do not carry over automatically. ## Honest boundaries S2Arm runs 64-bit (AArch64) games. Apple silicon cannot execute 32-bit ARM code, so 32-bit games are outside what S2Arm supports, as are games that need a 36-bit address space. ## Development [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [AI collaboration policy](LLM_POLICY.md) · [Diagnosis and root-fix skills for AI](skills/) · [Report a problem](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/issues) · [Third-party licenses](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md) ## Thanks S2Arm stands on the shoulders of its community. - **Co-developers**: thank you to everyone who has opened a pull request or issue in this project. Your code, device testing and bug reports shaped S2Arm (in order of first contribution): [@biglawine](https://github.com/biglawine), [@yyan160](https://github.com/yyan160), [@DanielZhangyc](https://github.com/DanielZhangyc), [@vickwv](https://github.com/vickwv), [@Xc1Ym](https://github.com/Xc1Ym), [@fjack](https://github.com/fjack), [@ha7rock](https://github.com/ha7rock), [@yourmoonlight](https://github.com/yourmoonlight), [@qidian99](https://github.com/qidian99), [@n06ody](https://github.com/n06ody), [@YTwsy](https://github.com/YTwsy), [@wdjwxh](https://github.com/wdjwxh), [@realskyrin](https://github.com/realskyrin), [@wwmogu](https://github.com/wwmogu), [@quancunlau](https://github.com/quancunlau), [@moongrant](https://github.com/moongrant), [@imyinyx](https://github.com/imyinyx), [@s-leeq](https://github.com/s-leeq), [@Zhangbu](https://github.com/Zhangbu), [@retX0](https://github.com/retX0), [@zh0ngtian](https://github.com/zh0ngtian), [@fengbird](https://github.com/fengbird), [@zsakvo](https://github.com/zsakvo), [@1500256797](https://github.com/1500256797), [@BossaMelon](https://github.com/BossaMelon), [@GayoZhao](https://github.com/GayoZhao), [@sovaly](https://github.com/sovaly), [@ruterfu](https://github.com/ruterfu), [@fyn1320068837-source](https://github.com/fyn1320068837-source), [@InTheManXG](https://github.com/InTheManXG). - **Ryujinx** (Ryujinx Team and Contributors, MIT): upstream for system services and shader translation; S2Arm's compatibility layer is built on it. - **[NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple)** (LNPANDY, MIT): upstream of the launcher interface. - **[nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)** (seedds, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 seedds): the original work behind the direct graphics layer that connects game graphics straight to Metal. That generous release is what made the direct path possible. - **[d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)** (MIT): pioneered this technical path, bringing your own Switch game natively to iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and HarmonyOS for the first time. - **Impactor** (Samara M, MIT) and **apple-codesign** (MPL-2.0): signing and installing from Windows. - **LNPANDY** and the original authors and contributors of the iOS library shell: the shell and its RomFS archive subsystem. - **ns2pro-bridge** (DanielZhangyc, MIT), **MacNativeGames** (MIT), **LumaDock** (MIT), **deko3d** (fincs, zlib), **nvn.h** (h1k421, MIT), **bcdec** (Sergii Kudlai, MIT / Unlicense), **SPIRV-Cross** and **Vulkan-Headers** (The Khronos Group), **SMAA** (Jorge Jimenez et al., MIT), the **Mesa** tessellator (Microsoft, MIT), **Capstone**, **LZ4**, **.NET**, **libvpx**, **libopus**, **dav1d**, and the **Noto** fonts. Versions, full license texts and what each component does are in [NOTICE](NOTICE) and the [third-party license list](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md). ## Star History ## License and legal S2Arm is open source under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The project ships no games and no keys; obtain your own game files legally. S2Arm is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, and game titles and trademarks belong to their respective owners.

# sheeridVerify · 教学与研究验证流程工作台

[![Tests](https://github.com/JenkinWoo/sheeridVerify/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JenkinWoo/sheeridVerify/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%3E%3D22.15-43853d)](https://nodejs.org/) [![License: ISC](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ISC-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**[sheeridVerify](https://github.com/JenkinWoo/sheeridVerify)** 是一个基于 Node.js 的验证流程学习项目，提供本地 Web 工作台、任务队列、浏览器表单交互及 HTTP 状态查询，供学校教学、学术研究和获得授权的流程测试使用。

> **用途说明：** 本项目仅以教学与研究为目的提供。使用真实平台前应取得必要授权，遵守适用法律和平台条款；不得伪造身份、学籍或材料，不得冒用信息、骗取权益或绕过资格审核。本项目与 SheerID 及任何学校均无官方隶属或认可关系，也不保证验证成功。详情见 [用途说明与免责声明](DISCLAIMER.md)，代码许可见 [ISC 协议](LICENSE)。

## 文档导航

- [快速开始](#快速开始)
- [工作台与接口说明](#使用)
- [Linux / Instabox 部署、更新与排错](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)
- [浏览器流程说明](docs/browser-workflow.md)
- [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [安全说明](SECURITY.md) · [免责声明](DISCLAIMER.md)

## 功能

- 通过 fetch 读取验证状态，按当前步骤选择浏览器或材料处理流程。
- 在 Web 页面创建、排队、停止、恢复和删除任务；失败任务删除后可重新提交。
- 按配置限制并发，记录任务进度，提交后默认每 5 秒查询结果。
- 上传原始 PNG、JPEG、PDF 文件，不生成或修改证明材料；交互式真人验证由用户完成。
- 使用访问密码、会话 Cookie、来源检查及写请求令牌保护工作台接口。

## 快速开始

需要 **Node.js >= 22.15** 与 npm。从 GitHub 获取源码：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JenkinWoo/sheeridVerify.git
cd sheeridVerify
```

使用下载的 ZIP 时，解压后进入其中包含 `package.json` 的目录。在项目根目录安装依赖与浏览器：

```bash
npm ci
npm run browser:install
```

首次使用时复制配置，已有个人配置请直接编辑原文件。

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
Copy-Item config/sheerid.example.json config/sheerid.local.json
```

Linux / macOS：

```bash
cp -n config/sheerid.example.json config/sheerid.local.json
```

编辑 `config/sheerid.local.json`，设置获授权的国家、学校、`data.organization.emailDomain` 和材料来源。该文件必须是标准 JSON，**不支持 `//` 注释或尾随逗号**。网页会按姓名和配置后缀生成邮箱，仅应使用自己有权使用的真实地址与资料。`document.path` 与 `document.url` 只能填写其中一个；示例配置不包含可直接提交的真实资料。

```bash
npm run web
```

打开 **http://127.0.0.1:8787**。本地默认访问密码为 `JenkinWoo`；对外开放前必须通过 `ONE_WEB_PASSWORD` 更换密码，并配置 HTTPS 入口。Linux 有界面浏览器需要可用桌面；完整部署步骤和环境变量模板见 [部署指南](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)。

## 测试与贡献

```bash
npm test
```

测试使用模拟接口及本地页面，不向真实验证接口提交数据。未安装 Camoufox 时会跳过浏览器相关用例；网页和浏览器改动应在安装浏览器后验证。GitHub Actions 在 Node.js 22、24 上运行不含已安装浏览器的测试。欢迎按 [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md) 提交问题和改进，报告前请删除个人资料、凭据及真实验证链接。

## 协议与责任说明

项目采用 [ISC License](LICENSE)，与 `package.json` 的协议声明一致。教学与研究是项目的预期用途，不额外收窄 ISC 的开源授权范围。软件按原样提供；第三方依赖和平台分别适用自己的许可和条款。请在使用前阅读完整的 [用途说明与免责声明](DISCLAIMER.md)。

## 工作原理

当前命令行先用 Node.js 内置 `fetch` 查询状态，再选择执行流程：需要填写学生资料时使用 Camoufox，需要材料验证时使用纯 `fetch` 接口。材料上传保持文件原始内容，不生成或修改证明文件。

## 使用

### 本机 Web 工作台

```powershell
npm run web
```

打开 **http://127.0.0.1:8787**。页面填写验证链接、名、姓、出生日期、代理和访问密码。`url`、`firstName`、`lastName`、`birthDate` 必须由创建任务接口传入，缺少时拒绝入队。邮箱不再由前端传入，而是每次根据配置文件中的 `emailDomain` 域名后缀按 `First name + 点 + Last name @xxx.edu`（如 `first.last@xxxx.edu`）格式自动拼接生成。国家、学校、材料来源、浏览器、超时、邮箱后缀等设置，每次启动任务时从 `config/sheerid.local.json` 读取；提交值不会写回配置文件。当前配置及示例配置不再保存验证链接和个人信息。

`POST /api/jobs` 的 JSON 请求体示例（认证仍使用会话 Cookie 或 `X-Web-Password`，写请求携带 `X-Local-Token`）：

```json
{
  "url": "https://services.sheerid.com/verify/项目ID/?verificationId=验证ID",
  "firstName": "Test",
  "lastName": "Student",
  "birthDate": "2000-01-02",
  "proxy": ""
}
```

当前配置用于 Web/API 模式。若单独使用 CLI，需通过 `--config` 指定含验证链接及所需资料的独立配置；`document.url` 仍是材料下载地址，继续保留在配置中。

代理填写时使用输入的代理，留空或只有空格时强制直连，**不使用配置中的代理、系统代理或代理环境变量**。支持 HTTP/SOCKS5 URL 及 `host:port:username:password`。`AUTOMATION_URL` 也不会覆盖网页输入的链接。

点击“加入队列”后，按入队顺序自动填写、提交，并按配置继续材料流程；`browser.autoFill: false` 时遵循原有手动填写模式。材料来源沿用配置中的 `document.path` 或 `document.url`，下载查询中的姓名使用本次网页输入。点击提交后保留浏览器，只有接口确认进入 `docUpload` 且没有终止错误时，才关闭浏览器并继续上传文件。

并发上限由 `config/sheerid.local.json` 的 `web.concurrency` 控制，默认 1。例如同时执行 3 个任务：

```json
"web": { "concurrency": 3 }
```

并发数必须是正整数，服务启动和新任务入队时读取；调低上限不会中断正在运行的任务，后续等到名额足够再启动。排队任务保存入队时的配置快照。任务使用链接中的 `verificationId` 作为唯一 ID；服务本次运行期间重复提交同一 ID 只返回已有任务，不会重复执行。已停止的任务可以通过“恢复任务”明确重新加入队尾，沿用原资料、代理及配置，重复点击不会重复入队；成功或失败的任务不能通过该按钮重跑。

右侧列出队列，点击任务可查看对应进度和日志；刷新保留选中的任务。表单可连续添加不同任务。停止排队任务会立即取消；停止运行任务会终止后续操作，并在对应浏览器和连接清理完成后释放并发名额，随后才可恢复。恢复时先检查远端验证状态；尚未确认的提交继续只读查询。保留浏览器等待手动操作的任务仍占用名额。停止 Web 服务会取消所有排队和运行任务；队列与历史仅保存在服务内存中，重启后不自动恢复或重试。

Web 默认仅监听本机，不把完整配置返回前端，也不持久保存输入的个人资料和代理密码。提交后的审核等待会继续占用任务名额，直到成功、失败或手动停止。

页面选中失败、已结束或已停止的任务后，可点击“删除当前任务”，再用相同链接重新加入队列。删除最后一个任务会清空进度和活动记录，表单内容继续保留；运行中的任务需先停止并等待资源清理完成。

删除历史任务接口：`DELETE /api/jobs/:verificationId`。请求携带已验证的会话 Cookie 或 `X-Web-Password`，以及 `X-Local-Token`（先通过 `GET /api/session` 获取 `token`），无需请求体。已完成、失败或已停止且清理完资源的任务可删除，成功返回 HTTP 200 和 `{ "id": "verificationId", "deleted": true }`；排队、运行或正在停止的任务返回 HTTP 409 / `JOB_ACTIVE`，请先调用 `POST /api/jobs/:verificationId/cancel` 并等待停止完成；不存在的任务返回 HTTP 404 / `JOB_NOT_FOUND`。删除只移除本服务内存中的任务及活动记录，不撤销验证平台上的提交，也不删除磁盘运行日志。删除后相同 ID 可通过正常创建任务接口重新入队，仍先检查远端状态。

网页只在有排队、运行或正在停止的任务时自动刷新进度；全部任务结束并读取最终日志后停止轮询。加入、恢复或切换任务会重新读取状态；已停止任务不会被反复查询。空闲页面要查看其他页面新建的任务时，刷新网页即可。

首次状态分流和浏览器启动前的检查遇到网络错误、超时或 HTTP 5xx 时最多尝试 3 次，重试间隔按 `polling.intervalMs` 递增（默认 5 秒、10 秒），等待可随任务停止而取消。HTTP 4xx（含 429）及无效响应在初始检查中直接停止。网页将状态查询失败、网络/代理异常、请求限流与真正的验证拒绝分别显示，避免把连接失败误报为“验证失败”；这些重试只用于只读状态查询。

### 提交后的状态跟踪

自动提交资料或材料后，程序继续通过 fetch 查询状态，默认每 5 秒一次。`pending`、`emailLoop` 都是中间状态，不结束任务；邮件步骤仍需用户完成邮件操作。正常提交流程最终返回 `verified`（成功）或 `failed`（失败），手动停止仍显示“已停止”。若只是查询现状，`npm run status` 仍只请求一次。

服务端重新返回 `docUpload` 且没有终止错误时，重新请求 `document.url` 获取当前原始文件（仍携带本次姓名），重新申请上传地址并提交；本地文件则重新读取。不会复用上次文件字节或上传地址。`rejectionReasons` 是退回材料的原因，`currentStep: error` 或非空 `errorIds`（包括 `docReviewLimitExceeded`）会终止失败。

可设置 `"polling": { "intervalMs": 5000 }`，范围 1000–300000 毫秒。审核没有人为设置的总等待超时，可通过停止按钮或 Ctrl+C 取消。查询暂时断网、超时或 HTTP 5xx 时退避重试；HTTP 429 仅在带 `Retry-After` 且没有终止错误时按指示等待。上传/提交响应丢失时先持续只读查询，不直接重放写请求；确认已进入审核后，才允许处理后续新的补交材料要求。不可恢复的接口/材料错误会标记任务失败；`submissionUncertain` 表示服务端结果尚未确认。

端口占用时使用 `npm run web -- --port 8788`。关闭服务按 Ctrl+C；不要关闭服务终端后继续操作 Web 页面。

### instabox 部署

程序目录为 `/data/workspace/one`，使用 Node.js 22+，运行 `npm ci` 和 `npm run browser:install` 安装依赖及对应平台的 Camoufox。Linux 有界面浏览器使用 `DISPLAY=:1`，可在 instabox 的 Computer 标签中查看和操作；个人配置仍使用 `config/sheerid.local.json`。

公网部署设置 `ONE_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`、`ONE_WEB_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://你的域名`，可用 `ONE_WEB_PASSWORD` 覆盖默认访问密码 `JenkinWoo`。不再使用 `ONE_WEB_USER` 或 HTTP Basic 登录；网页可直接打开，在表单的“访问密码”中输入密码即可。API 校验密码或会话 Cookie，并继续检查来源和写请求令牌。公网必须使用 HTTPS 入口；未配置监听环境变量时仍只监听本机。密码校验成功后设置 HttpOnly、SameSite=Strict 的会话 Cookie（公网额外设置 Secure），刷新页面无需重复输入；服务重启后需重新验证。

直接调用接口时，向 `GET /api/session` 发送 `X-Web-Password: JenkinWoo`（自定义密码时替换），保存返回的 `token`。后续 API 请求携带该密码头或返回的会话 Cookie；创建、停止、恢复、删除任务还需携带 `X-Local-Token: token`。默认密码仅存在于后端，页面不会预填密码。

`deploy/one-web.service` 可安装到 `~/.config/systemd/user/one-web.service`，凭据环境文件使用 `/data/workspace/one/.env.web`（权限 600）。使用 `systemctl --user enable --now one-web` 启动；修改代码后执行 `systemctl --user restart one-web`，日志使用 `journalctl --user -u one-web`。停止服务会结束任务；服务重启后队列为空。服务器重启后需保持用户服务运行，并在启动浏览器任务前确保 Computer 桌面可用。

### 命令行

要求 Node.js >= 22.15。默认读取 `config/sheerid.local.json` 的验证链接和材料来源；下载网络材料时可使用配置中的姓名查询原始文件。

```powershell
# 按状态分流：需要资料时打开浏览器并填写，但不提交；其他状态只报告
npm start
# 始终只查询状态，不开浏览器、不上传
npm run status

# 按当前状态提交：资料步骤走浏览器，材料步骤上传指定文件
npm run submit -- --file "C:\Documents\student-proof.png"

# 网络材料地址：保留引号，避免查询参数中的 & 被 shell 解析
npm run submit -- --url "https://school.example.edu/proof?id=123"

# 使用独立配置文件
npm run submit -- --config config/documents.local.json --file "C:\Documents\student-proof.pdf"
```

`--file` 和 `--url` 二选一，均覆盖配置中的材料来源。配置中可填写 `document.path`（本地路径）或 `document.url`（HTTP/HTTPS 地址），不能同时填写两个非空值；配置好后可直接使用 `npm run submit`，无需每次指定路径。旧的 `document.path` 配置继续有效。所有相对路径以启动命令时的工作目录为基准，Windows JSON 路径需写成双反斜杠或使用正斜杠。只有状态允许材料提交且指定了提交模式时才读取或下载材料，完整读取并通过检查后才发起任何验证状态写操作。

最小配置参考 `config/documents.example.json`：

```json
{
  "app": "sheerid",
  "url": "https://my.sheerid.com/rest/v2/verification/REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_VERIFICATION_ID",
  "document": { "path": "C:/Documents/student-proof.png" },
  "timeouts": { "apiMs": 20000, "downloadMs": 120000, "uploadMs": 120000 },
  "artifactsDir": ".runs"
}
```

使用网络材料时，将上面的 `document` 替换为：

```json
"document": { "url": "https://school.example.edu/proof?id=123" }
```

地址须直接返回原始 PNG、JPEG 或 PDF 内容。支持查询参数和内网 HTTP/HTTPS 地址；运行脚本的电脑必须能访问它。下载不携带浏览器 Cookie 或登录凭据，返回登录页、HTML 或 JSON 时会停止，不会继续上传。不会生成或修改材料内容。

配置了 `data.firstName` 和 `data.lastName` 时，下载 `document.url` 或 `--url` 会将去除首尾空格的姓名用一个空格连接，以 URL 编码写入 `name` 查询参数；例如 `?page=2` 变为 `?page=2&name=First+Last`。原有其他参数保留，已有 `name` 会替换为当前配置的姓名，用于查询对应的原始材料。独立材料配置未提供姓名时保留原地址；只提供部分姓名则停止下载并提示补全。本地文件不受影响，日志不记录姓名或完整下载地址。

URL 也可使用原来的 `https://services.sheerid.com/verify/<programId>/?verificationId=...` 页面链接。`AUTOMATION_URL` 环境变量可以覆盖 URL。每次从 URL 读取验证 ID，不在代码中写死。

支持 HTTP、HTTPS 和 SOCKS5 代理，包括账号密码认证。在本地配置增加顶层 `proxy`：

```json
"proxy": {
  "server": "http://proxy.example.com:8080",
  "username": "YOUR_USERNAME",
  "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD"
}
```

SOCKS5 使用 `"server": "socks5://proxy.example.com:1080"`，账号密码字段保持同样格式；无认证代理可省略这两个字段。也可将 `proxy` 写为字符串：`"http://user:password@host:port"`、`"socks5://user:password@host:port"`，或服务商提供的 `"host:port:username:password"`（未指定协议时默认 HTTP）。URL 中的特殊凭据字符需百分号编码；推荐使用分开的字段，避免手动编码。`sock5://` 兼容为 `socks5://`。

`AUTOMATION_PROXY` 环境变量可覆盖配置，格式与代理字符串相同；为空时使用配置。

未配置代理时（省略 `proxy`、`null`、空字符串，或 `server`/`username`/`password` 全为空的对象）默认使用当前系统代理：依次读取 `HTTPS_PROXY`、`ALL_PROXY`、`HTTP_PROXY` 环境变量（大小写均可），再读取 Windows“设置 → 网络 → 代理”中已启用的手动代理（注册表 `ProxyEnable`/`ProxyServer`，分协议设置时优先 https，其次 http、socks）。系统代理关闭或未设置时直连。不支持 PAC 自动配置脚本和系统代理的排除列表。需要强制直连时设置 `"proxy": "direct"`（或 `false`）。仅填写账号密码而不填 `server` 仍会报 `INVALID_PROXY`；系统代理地址无法解析时报 `INVALID_SYSTEM_PROXY`。示例配置不包含真实凭据。

浏览器页面的 HTTP/HTTPS 请求、状态预检查、远程材料下载（含重定向）、上传及提交接口共用该代理配置；本机回环材料地址直接访问本机服务。带认证的 SOCKS5 经仅监听 `127.0.0.1` 随机端口的本机转接服务供浏览器使用，远程 `fetch` 使用同一转接服务；代理不可用时请求失败，不自动改为直连。任务结束时释放连接和转接端口，保持浏览器窗口期间也保持代理服务。这个设置不是系统级 VPN；开启代理后，非回环内网材料地址也经上游代理访问，需要上游能访问该地址。不会自动更换账号中的会话参数或探测出口 IP。

需要自动打开表单时，必须提供完整验证页面链接和所需个人资料；只有状态接口 URL 无法确定对应的页面地址，会报告 `FORM_URL_REQUIRED`。Web/API 模式的页面链接、姓名、邮箱、出生日期来自创建任务请求；当前 `config/sheerid.local.json` 只保留其余设置。独立 CLI 材料配置用于只查状态或处理材料步骤。

默认入口先查询一次状态选择分支，各执行器获得任务锁后再查询一次。`npm run submit` 点击提交后保留浏览器，通过 fetch 跟踪状态；接口尚未离开资料步骤或暂时不可用时继续等待，不重复点击提交。只有接口明确返回无终止错误的 `docUpload` 才关闭浏览器并转交文件上传；SSO 转入材料步骤时也等待该接口确认。尚未出现上传步骤的待审核、邮件状态继续保留浏览器。提交模式成功、终止失败或手动停止时仍清理浏览器，不因 `keepOpen: true` 保留窗口。上传交接时日志记录 `browser_closed` / `DOCUMENT_HANDOFF`，任务锁和代理保留到最终结果。结果中的 `documentRunId` 关联材料流程记录。`npm start` 仍只填写，按 `keepOpen` 保留窗口；`npm run status` 只查询一次。

如果表单已经提交并进入材料步骤，可直接运行 `npm run submit -- --file ...` 或 `--url ...`，程序按最新状态上传，不重复填写表单。材料地址中的 `localhost`、`127.0.0.1` 和 `[::1]` 直连运行脚本的电脑；其他地址按配置使用代理，重定向后重新判断连接方式。

有界面模式使用跟随窗口尺寸的视口，调整或最大化窗口时不会继续固定使用生成的视口尺寸。下拉框按实际就绪状态操作：字段可用后，等待唯一匹配的选项出现、稳定且可点击，点击后确认菜单关闭和选中值，再填写下一项。国家选择会清空搜索过滤，并兼容国家代码、英文及中文页面标签，避免将 `United States` 当作中文选项的搜索词；月份也按页面语言匹配。学校搜索仍使用配置中的学校名称，不自动选择第一条结果。

慢网络下，每次候选项选择最多等待 `timeouts.readyMs`（默认 120000 毫秒），等待期间每 10 秒输出 `waiting_for_options`。需要更长等待可将该值设为 `180000`，最大 `300000`。等待超时或未确认选中会停止后续填写，并按原 `browser.keepOpen` 配置保留窗口；随机输入延迟不替代数据加载等待。

学校选项在异步刷新期间消失、替换或暂时不可点击时，会在同一等待期限内重新定位。每次点击检查和点击各最多等待 1.5 秒，短暂超时不会立即结束整个流程。点击尝试后先检查是否已选中；仅在菜单仍明确展开且目标选项重新就绪时重试选择，不重新输入搜索词或重开已关闭的菜单。等待日志中的 `code` 区分 `OPTIONS_LOADING` / `OPTIONS_RELOADING`（加载或刷新）、`OPTION_STABILIZING`（等待稳定）、`OPTION_CLICK_PENDING` / `OPTION_CLICK_RETRY`（点击阶段）、`OPTION_COMMIT_PENDING`（等待选中确认）。确认超时单独报告 `OPTION_NOT_COMMITTED`，不再误报成点击失败。这些重试仅用于选择表单选项，不用于表单提交或材料上传。

学校搜索输入完成后，若候选列表连续 5 秒保持不变、没有加载提示且没有匹配校名，会移到输入末尾删除一个字符，重新触发搜索，并记录 `SEARCH_RETRIGGERED`。同一次学校选择最多执行一次，仍使用原有的总等待期限及完整校名/校区匹配规则。正在加载、已尝试点击选项、输入内容被用户修改或输入框不可编辑时，不删除字符。

填写不再无限等待全部外部图片和 iframe 触发 `load`：打开页面后最多等待 15 秒 `load` 事件（超时记录 `page_load_slow` 并继续），然后要求国家、姓名、邮箱控件真正渲染完成——不透明（未处于淡入阶段）、未被加载遮罩覆盖、可用，且位置连续 1 秒不变——才开始填写；每个字段填写前也需稳定 300 毫秒。`waiting_for_fields` 日志中的 `NOT_PAINTED`、`COVERED`、`<settling>` 分别表示控件尚透明/隐藏、被遮挡、正在等待布局稳定。选中确认只检查该控件及其关联菜单，避免页面其他组件的加载标记造成无关等待；日志中的 `OPTION_MENU_OPEN`、`OPTION_VALUE_MISMATCH`、`OPTION_VALIDATION_PENDING` 分别表示菜单尚未关闭、显示值不匹配、控件校验尚未完成。

SheerID 选择学校后会将搜索输入框替换为只读学校文本框，原搜索框 ID 不再保留。学校分支优先识别这个已选控件，核对只读状态、完整学校/校区名称及校验状态；确认稳定后继续填写姓名等字段，不再等待已被移除的搜索框。仅输入了搜索文字仍不算选中。

浏览器启动时排除 Camoufox 自带的 uBlock Origin，减少验证资源被扩展拦截的可能性。填写完成后统一等待提交按钮：按钮禁用、被遮挡或页面显示“正在确认您是真人”时等待；出现“无法确认您是真人”和可用的“重试”按钮时点击重试，同一次运行最多 3 次。每次重试先等待加载结果，不连续点击；若错误提示始终未变化，至少间隔 5 秒才再尝试。第 3 次后再次失败，返回 `failed` / `HUMAN_VERIFICATION_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`，不提交表单。错误提示消失本身不算成功，必须等提交按钮可点击且没有验证加载/错误提示。

等待总预算由 `timeouts.humanMs` 控制，默认累计 180000 毫秒，最多可配置为 300000 毫秒；填写结束和提交前共用预算及重试计数，不会各自重试 3 次。持续加载或按钮始终不可点击时，达到预算即失败，即使尚未用完 3 次重试。日志每 10 秒报告等待原因，每次重试记录 `PAGE_RETRY_1_OF_3` 等计数。交互式真人验证由用户在浏览器中完成，脚本不会操作挑战内容。`npm start` 填写并等待按钮就绪后结束自动操作，仍不点击提交；只有提交模式会在就绪后提交一次。失败后按原 `keepOpen` 配置保留窗口。

## 状态与接口顺序

浏览器出现 “We couldn't continue your verification”（或对应中文标题 / `#sid-step-error` 错误页）时，立即按终止失败处理：`status: failed`、`code: VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE`，退出码 1。页面检测覆盖表单等待、填写、真人验证重试及提交后的结果等待；即使已经点击过提交，明确的错误页也不会被记成结果未知。不会点击该错误页上的 “Try again”，也不会新建验证会话；它与可重试三次的内联真人验证错误是两种状态。窗口仍按原 `keepOpen` 配置保留。

每次运行先请求 `GET https://my.sheerid.com/rest/v2/verification/{id}`，核对返回 ID、步骤和错误码。

| 当前状态 | 提交模式的行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `sso` 且无错误 | 先读取本地材料或下载网络材料并检查，再 `DELETE /step/sso`；仅当返回 `docUpload` 且无错误时继续 |
| `docUpload` 且无错误 | 读取本地材料或下载网络材料并检查，进入上传流程 |
| `collectStudentPersonalInfo` 且无错误 | 打开浏览器填写；`npm run submit` 还会点击提交，`npm start` 仅填写；不在这个步骤调用取消 SSO 或上传接口 |
| `success` | 返回 `verified`，不重复提交 |
| `pending` / `emailLoop` | 持续查询；邮件步骤等待用户完成邮件操作 |
| `error` 或非空 `errorIds` | 提交模式返回 `failed` 并停止，包括 `fraudRulesReject` |
| 未知步骤 | 提交模式返回 `failed` / `UNSUPPORTED_VERIFICATION_STEP`；只查状态仍报告 `not_actionable` |

上传流程为：

1. `POST /step/docUpload`：发送文件名、MIME 类型和实际字节数。本地来源使用原文件名；网络来源按内容命名为 `document.png`、`document.jpg` 或 `document.pdf`，不把查询参数带入文件名。
2. 从响应中的唯一文档记录获取 `uploadUrl`，验证它是 HTTPS S3/SheerID 地址。
3. `PUT uploadUrl`：发送原始文件字节及对应 `Content-Type`，不用 multipart，不附带 SheerID Cookie 或认证头。
4. PUT 成功后，`POST /step/completeDocUpload`，按接口返回的最终步骤记录结果。

支持本地和网络 PNG、JPEG、PDF，按文件头识别格式。本地来源还检查扩展名、普通文件类型及读取前后大小一致性；网络来源不依赖 URL 扩展名或响应文件名，下载时按实际接收字节累计检查大小，因此没有 `Content-Length` 也受限制。材料必须非空且不超过项目的 20 MiB 上限；这不是对服务端文件大小限制的保证，也不判断材料的真实性。网络读取仅在内存中缓冲，不另存到磁盘。

官方接口依据：[SheerID OpenAPI](https://services.sheerid.com/rest/v2/swagger.yaml)。其中 `DELETE /verification/{id}/step/sso` 的说明是取消 SSO 并转入 `docUpload`；并非跳过最终学籍审核，也不适用于尚在填写资料的步骤。

## 运行与结果

需要手动填写时，在本地配置的 `browser` 中设置 `"autoFill": false`，然后运行 `npm start`。默认值为 `true`，改回即可恢复自动填写。手动模式仍按当前验证状态决定是否打开表单；表单打开后跳过资料校验、字段等待、自动填写、真人验证重试及自动提交，保持窗口供你操作，关闭窗口或 Ctrl+C 后清理任务。需要 `headless: false` 且不能设置 `keepOpen: false`；此模式仅在资料填写步骤拒绝 `--submit`。手动提交进入材料步骤并关闭旧任务窗口后，可用 `--submit` 上传材料，无需重新开启自动填写；`--status` 仍只查询状态。

手动模式结果为 `status: manual` / `code: MANUAL_MODE`，只表示已打开页面交给用户，不表示填写完成或验证通过。后续手动填写、提交及验证结果以浏览器页面为准，`submissionAttempted` 只记录脚本是否提交。该开关不关闭网页自身的 JavaScript。

启动预检查或写请求遇到 HTTP 429 时仍报告 `API_RATE_LIMITED` 并停止。提交后的只读轮询仅在有 `Retry-After` 且响应未包含终止错误时等待并重试；没有恢复时间或已达到业务限制则失败，不连续重试。

状态和材料接口均通过 `fetch`。写请求不直接自动重试；只读轮询和服务端新要求的补交材料按上述规则处理。状态和上传接口不跟随重定向。网络材料下载最多跟随 3 次 HTTP/HTTPS 重定向，禁止 HTTPS 降级到 HTTP，不接受 URL 内嵌账号密码；超时覆盖整个下载和重定向过程。API 默认超时 20 秒，下载和上传各默认 120 秒，可分别配置 `timeouts.apiMs`、`timeouts.downloadMs` 和 `timeouts.uploadMs`。Ctrl+C 取消当前任务并释放任务锁。

标准错误输出阶段日志；标准输出返回最终 JSON。`.runs/<runId>.json` 保存状态、阶段和错误码，不保存材料字节、文件路径、材料源 URL、预签名上传 URL 或完整接口响应。每次远端写入前仍保存 `submission_unknown` 作为崩溃恢复记录；正常运行时响应丢失会继续只读查询，最终记录成功或失败。服务退出后不会自动重放未确认的提交。

材料分支结果中的 `remoteWriteAttempted` 记录是否已进入远端写入流程，`submissionAttempted` 记录是否进入完成上传请求；`browserOpened` 为 `false`。浏览器分支的 `submissionAttempted` 表示是否尝试点击提交，`browserOpened` 表示是否已创建浏览器会话。`pending` 表示等待审核，只有接口返回 `success` 才记录 `verified`。

| 结果 | 退出码 |
| --- | --- |
| `filled` / `verified` / `manual` | 0 |
| `failed` / `rejected` | 1 |
| `document_required` / `sso_required` / `personal_info_required` / `email_required` / `human_verification_required` / `pending` / `not_actionable` | 2 |
| `submission_unknown` | 3 |
| 用户中断 | 130 |

同一验证 ID 使用同一任务锁，包含与历史浏览器流程之间的互斥。旧浏览器任务仍运行时，应先正常关闭该任务。配置 `*.local.json`、`.runs/`、`documents/` 均被 Git 忽略。

## 模块与扩展

```text
src/cli.js                              按状态分流的命令行
src/core/workflow.js                    浏览器/材料接口分流
src/core/http.js                        fetch、超时、取消及错误处理
src/core/proxy.js                       代理配置解析，不在错误中暴露凭据
src/core/network.js                     任务级代理转接及 fetch 路由
src/apps/sheerid/client.js               状态和材料接口客户端
src/apps/sheerid/document.js             本地读取、网络下载与统一格式检查
src/apps/sheerid/document-workflow.js    状态机、任务锁及结果记录
src/core/config.js                      统一配置
src/core/storage.js                     锁及原子结果保存
```

```javascript
import { loadConfig, runDocumentWorkflow } from './src/index.js';
const config = await loadConfig('config/sheerid.local.json');
const status = await runDocumentWorkflow(config); // 只查询
// 有文件且确认需要提交时：
const result = await runDocumentWorkflow(config, {
  submit: true,
  file: 'C:/Documents/student-proof.png',
});
```

网络来源在上面的调用中用 `url: 'https://school.example.edu/proof?id=123'` 替换 `file`。统一分流库入口为 `runWorkflow(config, { submit, statusOnly, file, url, signal })`；这里的 `url` 是材料地址，验证地址仍由 `config.url` 提供。直接调用 `runDocumentWorkflow` 则始终只使用材料接口，遇到资料填写步骤返回 `personal_info_required`。浏览器分支调用 `runAutomation`，只有需要表单时才由 CLI 延迟加载 Camoufox；原随机输入、保持窗口和指纹配置仅作用于浏览器分支。更多浏览器设置见 [docs/browser-workflow.md](docs/browser-workflow.md)，历史命令说明以本 README 为准。

运行 `npm test` 可执行离线回归测试，覆盖浏览器到材料流程的衔接、任务锁、上传响应丢失、下载姓名参数及本机材料下载。有已安装的 Camoufox 时还会运行学校搜索的本地测试页；没有时跳过这些浏览器用例。测试不访问真实验证接口。

items.description: Let AI agents use your phone, with you in the loop.
items.readme:
Pinky

Let any AI agent use your iPhone or Android phone, from macOS, Windows or Linux, with you in the loop.

Download · Get started · FAQ · Discord

English · 简体中文 · 日本語


A real Claude Code run on an Android 16 emulator. Pinky asks before payments by default; this run also asks before messages.

Pinky lets any agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor or a script) operate a real iPhone or Android phone over MCP, while you watch on your computer, approve risky steps, take over and review what happened. Approvals are enforced by Pinky's gateway, not by instructions to the agent. - **Every platform.** One app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. It drives Android phones (Android 10 to 17) and iPhones on iOS 17.4 or later: nothing to install on iOS 27 and later, and a helper installed once from Xcode on iOS 17.4 to 26, which you can also choose on iOS 27 (tried there, on a phone below it and on Simulators; [details](#phones)). - **Tiny and native.** The window is drawn by [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) on the GPU, with no Electron and no webview: a 16–22 MB download that idles at about 70 MB of memory and 0% CPU on a Mac. - **Any agent, one click.** Settings › Agents connects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and more, and any agent that can use MCP servers works, on the same computer or over HTTP. - **Locked phone? Unlock it from your computer.** Save the phone's PIN in Pinky once, then confirm each unlock with Touch ID, Windows Hello or your keyring's password. Agents never see the PIN. - **Free and open source** under the Apache-2.0 license, with no account to create.

You approve the risky steps. Payments, trades and transfers wait for your click; in Settings › Safety you can have sends, orders, deletions, calls, installs, links that leave the app and settings changes wait too, or every step. Pinky spots these buttons in 10 languages. The rules run in Pinky's gateway, so an agent can't approve itself, even when text on the screen tries to talk it into it.
Off-limits by default. Banking, wallet and password-manager apps are invisible to agents, and agents can't type into password or one-time-code fields. When an agent needs a banking or wallet app for a task, it asks, and you can allow that app for that task only. Every new agent needs your approval and gets only the scope you give it.

Your phone stays yours. On Android 13 and later, agents work on a hidden second screen, so the phone's own screen stays yours, or off and locked. On older Android phones and on iPhones they use the main screen.
Take over any time. Click the mirror and the agent pauses until you hand back; on Android, touching the phone yourself pauses it too. Stop all is ⌥⌘. (Ctrl+Alt+. on Windows and Linux) from anywhere.

Every run is on the record. Each step in plain words, screenshots and a screen recording with a mark per step, exportable as an HTML report. It all stays on your computer.
iPhones too. The same gateway, approvals and records work on iOS 17.4 and later (what works). Shown here on the iOS Simulator, with deletions set to ask.
**Status:** pre-alpha. Claude Code has used real phones through it end to end (an Android phone over USB, an iPhone on iOS 27, and an iPhone XS Max on iOS 18.7.11 through the helper), and agents can connect over stdio or HTTP. Unlocking from the computer, background work on Android, recordings, export, Wi-Fi pairing and the phone's files are built; some of it still waits for a person to try it. See [docs/ACCEPTANCE.md](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md) for what works today and how to try it. ## Get started Install Pinky, connect your phone and add Pinky to your agent. Then ask the agent to do something on the phone, and watch it work in Pinky's window. ### What you need | | You need | | --- | --- | | **Mac** | macOS 13 or later, with Apple silicon or Intel | | **Windows** | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x64) | | **Linux** | A 64-bit PC (x86-64) with Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11 or a newer system (glibc 2.29 or later), and GTK 3 | | **Android phone** | Android 10 to 17 and a USB cable. Pinky brings its own adb; on Windows some phones need a USB driver, and on Linux USB access ([below](#usb-on-windows-and-linux)) | | **iPhone or iPad** | iOS 17.4 or later, and a USB cable to set it up; afterwards it works over Wi-Fi too ([below](#iphones-and-ipads-over-wi-fi)). Pinky prepares it itself, with Apple's developer disk image, which comes with Xcode or which Pinky can download from a third-party mirror when you ask ([below](#iphone)). On iOS 17.4 to 26 also a helper app on the iPhone ([below](#iphones-on-ios-174-to-26)) | | **Simulators and emulators** | Optional, in place of a phone or next to one: an iOS Simulator on a Mac with Xcode, or an Android emulator from Android Studio. You create them there; Pinky starts them ([below](#phones)) | | **Agent** | Any agent that can use MCP servers, such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex or Cursor | ### 1. Download and install Pinky Get Pinky from [the latest release](https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky/releases/latest): - **Mac:** download `pinky--arm64.dmg` for a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) or `pinky--amd64.dmg` for an Intel Mac. Open it and drag Pinky to Applications. With [Homebrew](https://brew.sh), `brew install --cask diygod/tap/pinky` does the same. - **Windows:** download `pinky-setup--amd64.exe` and run it. It installs Pinky for your account, without administrator rights. The installer is not signed yet, so SmartScreen may say that Windows protected your PC: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. To use Pinky without installing it, unzip `pinky--windows-amd64.zip` and open `Pinky.exe`. - **Linux:** on Debian and Ubuntu, download `pinky__amd64.deb` and install it with `sudo apt install ./pinky__amd64.deb`. On other systems, unpack `pinky--linux-amd64.tar.gz` into a folder of its own and run `pinky` in it. Pinky looks for new versions by itself and, on a Mac, with the Windows installer and unpacked from the Linux `.tar.gz`, installs them too ([Updates](#updates)). ### 2. Connect your phone Open Pinky and choose **Add phone**. A phone that is ready shows up in Pinky's window; when something is missing, the phone's page in Pinky says what. #### Android **Add phone › Android** shows these steps for your phone's brand, with its own menu names and extra switches: Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, HONOR, HUAWEI, Samsung and Pixel, and general steps for the rest. 1. On the phone, turn on USB debugging: in Settings › About phone, tap **Build number** 7 times, then turn on **USB debugging** in Settings › System › Developer options. Some brands name these menus a little differently. 2. Plug the phone into the computer. When the phone asks whether to allow USB debugging, tap **Allow**. On Android 11 and later you can pair it over Wi-Fi instead, from **Add phone** ([when it fails](#when-pairing-over-wi-fi-fails)). Android 10 has no Wireless debugging: once it is plugged in, **Use Wi-Fi instead…** moves it to Wi-Fi ([below](#phones)). 3. Pinky offers to install Pinky Companion, its app for the phone, which makes reading the screen many times faster and lets Pinky type in any language. The phone may ask you to allow the install once. Each phone has a **Checkup**, in the ··· menu under its mirror, that lists what works and how to fix what doesn't, such as a Xiaomi's USB debugging (Security settings) switch. Over Wi-Fi, Pinky makes sure the phone that answers is yours: it leaves a mark on each phone it sets up, which only the phone's debugging connection can read, and checks it whenever adb connects the phone, so another device on the network can't answer in its place. A phone connected over Wireless debugging that Pinky hasn't used, by another tool for example, shows as found on Wi-Fi, and Pinky leaves it alone until you choose **Use**. If a phone's page says **This may not be …** after you reset the phone or set it up again yourself, choose **Trust this phone…** there, or plug it in once. Taking the phone out? With Tailscale, Pinky reaches it away from home too ([how](#phones-away-from-home)).

Add phone › Android, with a Xiaomi picked.
A Redmi's Checkup, with two things to fix.
#### Android tools Pinky brings its own adb, the tool it reaches Android phones with, built from Android's source, so nothing else needs installing. When the computer has Android's platform tools already, from Android Studio, Homebrew or the system's packages, Pinky uses those, and shares their adb server with Android Studio and other tools. When Pinky quits, it stops the adb it brought, unless another app such as Android Studio is using it; Settings › Advanced › **Stop adb when Pinky quits** turns that off. An adb you installed keeps running. #### USB on Windows and Linux - **Windows:** the phone's USB debugging needs a driver. Windows installs one by itself for many phones; when it has none, Pinky lists the phone as needing setup and says which driver to install: the [Google USB Driver](https://developer.android.com/studio/run/win-usb) for Pixels, [Samsung's](https://developer.samsung.com/android-usb-driver) for Samsung phones, the [phone maker's](https://developer.android.com/studio/run/oem-usb) for others. Unplug the phone and plug it in again afterwards. - **Linux:** the computer must let Pinky open the phone's USB device, which takes udev rules for Android phones: `sudo apt install android-sdk-platform-tools-common` on Debian and Ubuntu, `android-udev` on Arch, `android-tools` on Fedora. You may also need to be in the `plugdev` group. Then plug the phone in again. Pinky says so when they are missing. #### When pairing over Wi-Fi fails When a phone works on the cable but **Pair over Wi-Fi** does not finish, the pairing page says within half a minute what Pinky sees: - **The phone hasn't shown up on the network yet:** check that Wireless debugging is on and that the phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the computer. Guest Wi-Fi, routers with AP (client) isolation and many office networks keep devices from finding each other. There, choose **Pair with a code instead**: on the phone, tap **Pair device with pairing code** and enter the IP address and port and the six-digit code it shows, which change each time that dialog opens. Pinky then needs no search to pair; if it still cannot find the phone afterwards, it asks for the IP address and port at the top of Wireless debugging (not the pairing dialog's) and connects there. If it cannot reach the phone at those addresses either, the network keeps its devices apart: use a Wi-Fi where they can reach each other, such as your home network rather than its guest network, or the cable. - **Pinky isn't allowed to look for phones on this network:** on a Mac, Pinky needs Local Network access, and macOS gives no error without it: the search just finds nothing. Choose **Open Local Network settings**, turn on Pinky under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network and try again (if macOS asks whether Pinky may find devices on your local network, click **Allow**). On a Mac, a phone's **Checkup** shows this too, under **Local network**. On Windows and Linux, a firewall can block the search the same way: let Pinky use the local network, or pair with a code. - **Pinky can't look for phones on this network:** check that the computer is connected to Wi-Fi or Ethernet. - **The phone showed up, but pairing hasn't finished:** if the phone shows an error or went back to Wireless debugging, scan the code again, or pair with a code. When pairing stops with an error, the page says what adb reported: - **The phone ended the pairing before it finished** (QR code): the phone left its scanning screen, changed Wi-Fi, or something between it and the computer cut the connection; adb cannot tell which. Keep the phone on the scanning screen and try again, or choose **Pair with a code instead** next to the message. - **The phone didn't accept the pairing** (pairing code): a wrong code, or a port that is not the pairing dialog's. The address at the top of Wireless debugging is for connecting, not pairing, and adb answers the same way for both mistakes. - **Nothing at that address is waiting to pair** or **The phone stopped waiting to pair:** the pairing dialog or the scanning screen closed, or the port is wrong. Open it again and use what it shows now. - **Couldn't reach the phone at that address** or **Pinky couldn't connect to it:** the network keeps the computer and the phone apart, as above; a VPN or firewall on the computer can too. - **The adb server running on this computer is too old:** another program started an adb older than platform-tools 30. Quit it, or update it, and Pinky starts its own. Pinky writes adb's own words to its log, which **Help › Send Feedback…** attaches with the diagnostics. Pairing over Wi-Fi needs Android 11 or later; an Android 10 phone moves to Wi-Fi from the cable instead (**Use Wi-Fi instead…**, [below](#phones)). Up to Android 16, Wireless debugging turns itself off when the phone leaves the Wi-Fi network, even for another access point of it, or restarts: turn it on again, or pair again from **Add phone**. #### iPhone Pinky prepares an iPhone itself; **Add phone › iPhone** walks you through it. 1. Plug the iPhone into the computer, unlock it, tap **Trust** and enter its passcode. On Windows, install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store (or iTunes) first; on Linux, the `usbmuxd` package. Add phone says when they are missing. 2. On the iPhone, turn on **Developer Mode** in Settings › Privacy & Security: Pinky makes the switch appear there. The iPhone restarts; unlock it, tap **Turn On** and enter the passcode. 3. Pinky mounts Apple's developer disk image on the iPhone and lists it as ready. An iPhone on iOS 27 keeps the image when it restarts; below iOS 27 Pinky mounts it again after each restart, once you unlock the iPhone. The developer disk image comes with [Xcode](https://apps.apple.com/app/xcode/id497799835), Apple's free app for developers, and Pinky does not ship it. On a Mac, install Xcode once and open it: Pinky uses the image it installs, and Xcode never has to run again. An iPhone on iOS 27 or later needs the image of Xcode 27 or later: Apple's signing server no longer signs older ones, and Add phone then says which image Pinky used and how to get a newer one. On Windows and Linux, copy `/Library/Developer/DeveloperDiskImages/iOS_DDI` from such a Mac into Pinky's folder ([where](docs/notes/ios.md#preparing-a-phone-without-xcode)). Without either, or when Apple refuses the image Pinky found (Xcode's, or one copied into Pinky's folder), Add phone offers to download the image from a third-party mirror, github.com/doronz88/DeveloperDiskImage (Xcode 27.0 beta 4, 32 MB, kept by the author of pymobiledevice3, not by Apple), only when you click Download; Pinky checks every file against the checksum it expects, and from then on uses it instead of an image Apple refused. On iOS 27 and later, no app gets installed on the iPhone. Checked on the iPhone 13 mini (iOS 27.0.1): Pinky mounting Xcode's image itself (in about 1.5 s, after the image had been taken off), keeping the image already on the phone, and that the iPhone keeps the image when it restarts. Not yet tried on a phone: the downloaded image, the Developer Mode switch, iPhones below iOS 27, and pairing an iPhone on Windows. Contributors have used an iPhone and an iPad on iOS 27.2 on Linux (Arch Linux), and an iPhone on iOS 27.2 on Windows 11, on the cable and over Wi-Fi, with the image already on them. #### iPhones and iPads over Wi-Fi Pinky also uses an iPhone or iPad over Wi-Fi while it is on the same Wi-Fi as the computer, and the computer lists it there, which it does once Wi-Fi connections are on for the phone. Pinky turns them on when you plug the phone in and it trusts the computer: it is the same setting as Finder's **Show this iPhone when on Wi-Fi**, so a phone already set up that way stays as it is. It is on by default; **Settings › Phones › Use iPhones and iPads over Wi-Fi** turns it off, which leaves the phones' setting alone. If a phone doesn't show up on Wi-Fi when you unplug it, its **Checkup** says where it stands under **Wi-Fi**: whether its Wi-Fi connection is on and whether Pinky turned it on, why Pinky couldn't, and whether this computer sees the phone on Wi-Fi. - An iPhone or iPad Pinky has used keeps working when you unplug it, as the same phone with its settings: Pinky moves it to Wi-Fi by itself, and back to the cable when you plug it in, and an agent's task goes on; its calls wait a few seconds meanwhile. - One Pinky has not used, such as a family member's iPad paired with this computer, shows as **Found on Wi-Fi**. Pinky reads its name, model and iOS version and does nothing else, and agents don't see it, until you choose **Use**, which sets it up over Wi-Fi, or **Ignore**, which keeps it off the list until you plug it in. - A locked iPhone or iPad on Wi-Fi shows as **Locked on Wi-Fi**, and Pinky connects to it once you unlock it: while it sleeps it drops off the network every minute or so, and connecting to it then lights its screen. - Setting one up over Wi-Fi: trusting the computer needs the cable, and so does making the Developer Mode switch appear while it is hidden (on a phone used with Xcode it shows already). Turning Developer Mode on happens on the phone, and Pinky mounts the developer disk image over Wi-Fi too, in about 9 s instead of 1.5 s. **Add phone › iPhone** says which step needs the cable. - Over Wi-Fi, Pinky talks only to the phone it paired with: it checks the certificate the phone got when it first trusted this computer, so another device on the network can't answer in its place. Below iOS 27, the WebDriverAgent helper's connection isn't encrypted, so there it is only as safe as the Wi-Fi. Over Wi-Fi each step is slower than on the cable, screenshots most of all. Measured on an iPad Pro 11-inch (3rd generation, iPadOS 27.0.1), Wi-Fi against the cable: a swipe shows on screen after 80 to 210 ms (60 to 90 ms), the home screen reads in 0.6 to 2.6 s (0.5 to 0.6 s), a screenshot takes 5 s (1 s), and 0.2 % of the video's packets were lost (none). Unplugging moved a running task to Wi-Fi in about 5 s, and plugging in moved it back in 2 to 6 s ([details](docs/notes/ios.md#wi-fi)). On a Mac, the system's device service, usbmuxd, can lose an iPhone on Wi-Fi after its connection broke once (its Wi-Fi turned off and on, say), and not look for it again for up to about an hour; Finder loses it too. Pinky notices when a phone you use is on the network but no longer listed, shows it as **Lost on Wi-Fi**, and offers **Restart device service…** on its page: after you confirm, macOS asks for an administrator's password, and every iPhone and iPad, also on a cable, disconnects for a second or two. `sudo killall usbmuxd` in Terminal does the same. Right after you unplug a phone it says so within about 10 seconds; it waits a minute otherwise, as a phone that wakes comes back by itself. A phone you unplug that this computer doesn't see on Wi-Fi at all shows as **Not seen on Wi-Fi**, with what may hide it: it's asleep, on another network or one that keeps devices apart (guest networks, some routers), a VPN, or Pinky not allowed on the local network. On Linux and Windows, the system's device service does not list iPhones and iPads on Wi-Fi by itself: on Linux (the `usbmuxd` package) it lists them only on the cable, and on Windows (Apple Devices or iTunes) only while they are on the cable too. So there Pinky runs a small device service of its own in front of the system's, while it uses phones over Wi-Fi: it finds the phones paired with this computer on the network and connects to them directly, and passes everything about phones on a cable to the system's. All of Pinky's connections to iPhones and iPads go through it then, on the cable too. There is nothing to install or set up for it beyond the system's own (`usbmuxd` on Linux, Apple Devices on Windows). If you run a device service that lists phones on Wi-Fi itself, such as netmuxd, and start Pinky with `USBMUXD_SOCKET_ADDRESS` pointing at it (`unix:///path/to/socket` or `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`), Pinky uses that one instead and runs none of its own. While Pinky opens a phone, or moves it between the cable and Wi-Fi, it shows **Connecting** or **Moving to Wi-Fi** rather than offline. Over Wi-Fi Pinky reads text from the live picture rather than from screenshots, which take about 5 s there. An iPhone or iPad without a passcode never reads as locked, so after it has dropped off the network to sleep, Pinky connects to it only once it has been back for 30 seconds. #### iPhones on iOS 17.4 to 26 Below iOS 27, an iPhone takes taps and typing from a computer only through a helper app on the phone: WebDriverAgent, which you build and install once from Xcode with your Apple ID ([how](docs/notes/ios.md#installing-the-webdriveragent-helper)). With a free Apple ID it has to be installed again every 7 days: two days before, the phone's page and its checkup remind you, and once it has run out the phone shows as needing setup and says why ([how to install it again](docs/notes/ios.md#when-the-helpers-signature-runs-out)). It has been tried on an iPhone XS Max on iOS 18.7.11, on Windows, over its cable and Wi-Fi. Without it, Pinky can only show and read the screen (on a Mac) and open apps: no taps, swipes or typing. iOS 17.3 and earlier are not supported. ### 3. Add Pinky to your agent In Pinky, open **Settings › Agents** and click **Connect** next to your agent. Pinky finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Copilot CLI, Windsurf (Devin Desktop) and Gemini CLI on your computer and adds itself to the agent's MCP servers, by the app's own path: with the agent's own command where it has one, such as `claude mcp add`, or in its settings file, which Pinky copies first and changes only in Pinky's entry. It also installs Pinky's agent guide, [SKILL.md](docs/SKILL.md), where the agent reads skills, and keeps it current: when Pinky updates, it rewrites the guide it installed to the new version's. Until an agent is connected, a card in Pinky's sidebar offers to do it, or says where to get one.

- **Claude Desktop:** Connect opens Pinky's extension in Claude Desktop; click **Install** there. Double-clicking `pinky-.mcpb` from the [release page](https://github.com/DIYgod/pinky/releases/latest) does the same. - **Other agents:** **Settings › Agents › Add an agent by hand** shows the command for your copy of Pinky, with buttons that copy it. Add an MCP server (stdio) that runs it. In a JSON config, with the Homebrew cask or a Linux package: ```json { "mcpServers": { "pinky": { "command": "pinkyctl", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Claude Code in a terminal: `claude mcp add --scope user pinky -- pinkyctl mcp`. Most agents read the guide from `~/.agents/skills/pinky/SKILL.md`, Claude Code from `~/.claude/skills/pinky/SKILL.md`. The command is `pinkyctl`, not `pinky`: many computers already have another program named `pinky`. An agent on another computer or in a container can connect over HTTP instead ([how](docs/mcp.md#over-http)). [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md#connecting-an-agent) says what Connect changes for each agent. ### 4. Try it Ask the agent to do something on your phone, for example "Open Messages on my phone and tell Sam I'm running late." The first time an agent connects, Pinky asks whether to allow it and what it may do. Payments wait for your click in Pinky's window; in Settings › Safety you can have sends, deletions and more wait too. No phone at hand? Start an iOS Simulator or an Android emulator in **Add phone › Virtual phone** ([below](#phones)). Or quit Pinky and start it with two scripted demo phones (a payment to approve, a blocked banking app, a password field): `/Applications/Pinky.app/Contents/MacOS/Pinky --fake` on a Mac, `pinkyctl --fake` on Linux, or `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Pinky\Pinky.exe" --fake` in PowerShell on Windows. ## Using Pinky ### Phones - **Android:** connected over USB or Wi-Fi ([above](#android)). Pinky works over adb and a bundled scrcpy server. Its companion app, which ships with Pinky, reads the screen in about 70 ms instead of 2 s and types any language without the clipboard: the phone's page offers to install it (the phone may ask you to allow it once). Its accessibility service is on only while an agent works on the phone, as banking apps refuse to run next to one ([why](#faq)). On Android 13 and later, agents work on a background display, so the phone's own screen can stay off and locked. Text that an app draws without describing it to the accessibility tree, as in mini-programs and other web pages inside super-apps, games and maps, is read from the screen's pixels (OCR) on macOS and Windows, so agents can read it and tap it. Pinky reads a blocked app this way only once you allow it for the task, never a locked phone, and keeps no picture. - **Wi-Fi on Android 10:** Android 10 has no Wireless debugging. Plug the phone in and choose **Use Wi-Fi instead…** in the ⋯ menu under its picture (or in Settings › Phones): Pinky has the phone's adb listen on the network (`adb tcpip`, port 5555), connects to it at its Wi-Fi address and says when you can unplug it. It connects again by itself when the phone is back on the network, also at a new address. While it is on, any computer on the same network can try to connect to the phone: if the phone asks **Allow USB debugging?** when you are not connecting it yourself, tap **Cancel**, and use it only on Wi-Fi you trust. It lasts until the phone restarts; then plug it in once and choose **Use Wi-Fi again**. **Stop the Wi-Fi connection** in the same menu turns it off ([details](docs/away-from-home.md#wi-fi-without-wireless-debugging)). - **iPhone:** connected over USB or Wi-Fi ([above](#iphones-and-ipads-over-wi-fi)) and prepared by Pinky ([above](#iphone)); iPads work the same way. Pinky reads on the iPhone when it runs out: two days before, the phone's page and its checkup remind you to install the helper again from Xcode, and once it has run out the phone shows as needing setup and says why, instead of failing to start the helper ([how](docs/notes/ios.md#when-the-helpers-signature-runs-out)). - **Screen sharing on iPhone:** while Pinky streams an iPhone's screen, iOS tells apps that the screen is being shared, and some banking apps (DBS digibank and China Merchants Bank among them) refuse to run or warn you. iOS also keeps the camera and microphone from apps then, so the camera shows black and scanning a code fails. Pinky streams it while the phone's page or tile is open in Pinky, while an agent works on it, and for 30 seconds after; then such apps work again. Over CoreDevice, agents cannot use them. Install the WebDriverAgent helper as well, and leave the phone on Automatic (Settings › Phones): tasks use CoreDevice, and Pinky moves a task to the helper, which shares no screen, when it opens DBS digibank or China Merchants Bank, or when the agent asks for it; the phone goes back to CoreDevice after the task. Or connect the iPhone through the helper for every task. - **Simulators and emulators:** an iOS Simulator (on a Mac with Xcode) or an Android emulator (from Android Studio) can be a phone too. **Add phone › Virtual phone** lists the ones on the computer: **Start** starts one, and once it runs it shows up as a phone, marked Simulator or Emulator; **Shut down** stops it. An Android emulator Pinky starts has no sound, so it never switches a Bluetooth headset to its microphone. Only you start them: agents have no tool for it. The live picture, recordings, approvals and rules work as on a phone. Pinky finds the Android SDK the way Android Studio does (`ANDROID_HOME`, then `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, then where Android Studio installs it), and an emulator then works like an Android phone on a cable. For Simulators, Pinky builds Appium's WebDriverAgent with your Xcode the first time: from the source of one release, whose files it checks before building, unsigned and without an Apple ID. That takes 20 seconds to a few minutes, and the build is kept until Xcode changes. Pinky creates no Simulators or emulators and downloads no system images: create them in Xcode (Window › Devices and Simulators) or in Android Studio's Device Manager ([details](docs/notes/ios.md#ios-simulators)). - **Locked phones:** Pinky never keeps a phone awake. It wakes the screen before a step; save the phone's PIN in Settings › Phones to unlock it from the computer with Touch ID. Agents never see the PIN. On Android this is checked on AOSP-style lock screens (LineageOS on a Mi 10 Pro, the Android 10, 16 and 17 emulators); the lock screens of Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO, OnePlus, vivo, Honor and Huawei are only covered by tests made from what is known of them, and where Pinky cannot read the PIN pad with confidence it enters nothing ([details](docs/notes/integration.md#unlocking-other-android-phones)). - **Pinching:** agents pinch to zoom maps, photos and pages in and out, and turn them with two fingers. You can too, on the phone's picture in Pinky: pinch on the trackpad (on Linux, under Wayland only), or drag with Option held (Alt on Windows and Linux), as in Xcode's Simulator, and a second finger moves opposite the pointer across the screen's centre. Like any touch of yours, it pauses the agent. iPhones pinch through the WebDriverAgent helper; through Device Hub (iOS 27 without the helper) they cannot, and agents are told so. - **Dragging:** agents drag with `phone_drag`: press and hold to pick something up, move through the points they name, rest where needed, and let go. They move app icons to another home screen page (resting near the screen's edge turns the page) or into a folder, reorder lists and move sliders. The rules and approvals treat a drag like a swipe, checking what lies under every point the finger touches, and the approval's screenshot draws the whole route. It works on Android and on iPhones through Device Hub or the WebDriverAgent helper. Tried on an Android emulator and an iOS Simulator, not yet on a phone. - **Files:** on Android, agents copy files between the phone's Pinky folder (`/sdcard/Pinky`, the only place on the phone they may reach) and a folder on the computer, and copying to the phone asks you first. Pictures copied there show in the phone's gallery and photo pickers, so an agent can attach them in a chat app. An agent on another computer cannot reach that folder, so it sends Pinky the file first: small files in the call, larger ones to a one-time link Pinky gives it. Copying the file to the phone then asks you as usual ([details](docs/mcp.md#uploading-a-file)). Not on iPhones. - **Screenshots and reports for bug reports:** an agent testing an app can save a screenshot as a file, and, as the task ends, the task's report (its steps with screenshots, as HTML and JSON), to put in a bug report or a pull request. They go into the phone's folder on the computer, on iPhones too, and saving asks nothing, as nothing on the phone changes. They show only what the agent may see: codes covered, nothing of a locked phone or a blocked app, even one you allowed for the task. The task's screen recording covers neither codes nor blocked apps, so it goes to the agent only when you allow it: when the agent exports a recorded task, Pinky asks you whether it gets the recording too (an MP4 next to the report), every time, and no preset or Always allow answers that for you. If you decline or don't answer, the agent gets the report alone. An agent on another computer gets a one-time link for each file ([details](docs/mcp.md#saving-screenshots-and-reports)). - **Links:** agents open links with `phone_launch`: web pages, an app's own links (`myapp://…`), and links for calls, texts and email. A build signed by someone else, or another app, still asks, and uninstalling asks every time. Pinky's own apps, system apps, finance apps, password managers and apps you blocked can't be installed over, uninstalled or stopped ([details](docs/mcp.md#phone_app)). - **App logs:** an agent testing an app can read that app's own log lines and crash reports, to see why it failed. The first time in a task, Pinky asks you (**Allow for this task** covers the rest of it, and **More options › Always allow** stops asking for that agent, phone and app until you take it back in Settings › Safety), unless the app is a development build (a debug build on Android, an app Xcode installed on an iPhone). Agents get only that app's lines, never other apps' or the system's, and never the logs of blocked, banking, wallet or password-manager apps, the phone's own apps or Pinky's. History keeps how many lines were read, not the lines. An iPhone keeps no log history Pinky can read, so there Pinky listens from the agent's first read until the task ends ([details](docs/mcp.md#phone_logs)). - **Testing an app:** agents can flip the switches developers test with: turn the screen, switch between light and dark appearance, simulate a location, and open an app in another language and region. Pinky puts everything back when the task ends, and leaves alone what you changed yourself meanwhile. Rotation and appearance work on Android and on iPhones with the helper; a simulated location on Android emulators, iOS Simulators and iPhones with the helper; another language on Android 13 and later and on iPhones ([details](docs/mcp.md#phone_device)). Its tasks, screenshots and recordings stay in Activity unless you tick the box to delete them too, and a task running on it stops. A phone on a cable comes back at once, as a new phone, until you unplug it. A phone on Wi-Fi is disconnected and stays off the list, even when adb connects it again by itself; to add it back, pair it again in Add phone or plug it in. An iPhone or iPad on Wi-Fi stays off the list until you plug it in. A task on it ends, agents are told it is paused, and Pinky does not reconnect it over Wi-Fi. It stays paused when Pinky restarts. Resume it with **Resume** on its page or **Resume connection** in its right-click menu, or plug it in by cable. A phone paused while plugged in stays paused until you unplug it and plug it in again, so pausing a phone that charges does not undo itself.
